Abstract: Indoor floorplan reconstruction from 3D point clouds is a fundamental task for digital twin and architectural modeling. However, fully supervised approaches heavily rely on exhaustive polygon-level annotations, which are notoriously time-consuming and labor-intensive to acquire. To address this bottleneck, we propose SyneFloor, a weakly supervised framework that achieves accurate floorplan reconstruction under extreme label scarcity. First, to overcome the structural degradation caused by sparse supervision, we extract robust instance-aware structural priors by leveraging the zero-shot segmentation capabilities of vision foundation models (e.g., SAM3). We then propose an Adaptive Mask-Query Synergistic Fusion (AMQSF) module to dynamically fuse these explicit geometric priors into Transformer queries. Second, to maximize the data efficiency of the limited annotation budget, we design a stage-wise, multi-criteria active learning strategy. By comprehensively evaluating predictive uncertainty and architectural complexity, the model actively selects the most informative and challenging scenes for annotation. Third, to fully exploit the remaining unannotated data, we introduce a topology-aware pseudo-label generation mechanism within a dual-network collaborative framework. By explicitly detecting and resolving topological conflicts, this mechanism produces high-quality, structurally valid pseudo-labels, which fundamentally guarantees the robustness of the semi-supervised learning process. Extensive experiments on the synthetic Structured3D and real-world SceneCAD datasets demonstrate the superiority of SyneFloor. It not only exhibits robustness by consistently outperforming current state-of-the-art methods under extreme label scarcity (1% to 10% budgets), but also matches or surpasses several 100% fully supervised methods with much less labeled expenditure (e.g. utilizing only 40% of labels). This dual capability thereby establishes a highly scalable and annotation-efficient paradigm for automated indoor floorplan reconstruction in practical applications. © 2026 International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, Inc. Abstract: Container ports are pressured for efficiency while reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions under decarbonization rules. Simulation-based operational planning frameworks are increasingly being explored for container terminal decarbonization and coordination analysis. This study fills the gap by developing a trace-driven offline digital twin (DT) framework integrated with a discrete event simulation model decision support for tactical planning and emissions assessment at Tanjung Priok International Container Port. Historical terminal operating system data were used to reproduce real operational conditions and evaluate alternative operational strategies without disrupting live terminal operations. Using deterministic simulations, the effects of coordination strategies, such as yard allocation, equipment deployment, and truck–vessel synchronization, on crane productivity, turnaround time, equipment utilization, and emissions were analyzed. The strategies impacted productivity, truck turnaround time, equipment utilization, and lifecycle GHG emissions. Monte Carlo simulations, the uncertainty and variability of environmental outcomes under different operational conditions were analyzed. The results show that coordination-based strategies outperform simple expansion in reducing congestion and emissions. Truck–vessel synchronization strategies and workload redistribution across yard space and time provide substantial operational and environmental benefits. The proposed framework should therefore be interpreted as a trace-driven offline DT discrete event simulation environment for tactical scenario evaluation rather than a fully synchronized real-time digital twin. © 2026 by the authors.

Abstract: Rendering high-fidelity 3D scenes is crucial for immersive applications like virtual reality and digital twins. However, standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) relies heavily on multi-view consistency, making it fragile in real-world scenarios plagued by glass reflections. These reflections often manifest as geometric "floaters"or severe texture artifacts, obscuring the true background. Existing solutions, which typically employ single-image priors or NeRF-based in-painting, often lack explicit 3D constraints or rely on synthetic data, failing to generalize to complex environments. To address these challenges, we first present a novel benchmark dataset of 8 real-world scenes, capturing physically paired reflective and reflection-free images. Building on this, we propose GlassSplat, a robust framework designed to eliminate view-dependent artifacts and recover clean transmission geometry. Our method initializes with a reflection prior and introduces an Affine-Based Exposure Correction module to align global photometric inconsistencies. To distinguishing valid geometry from virtual outliers, we incorporate an Epipolar Consistency Loss and an uncertainty-weighted Depth Regularization. Finally, to physically purge residual noise, we devise a Visibility-Aware Pruning strategy that dynamically filters artifacts based on multi-view statistics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GlassSplat significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, effectively recovering a clean, artifact-free 3D scene representation.  © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

Abstract: The upscaling of wind turbines (WTs) and the expansion of offshore and floating deployment are turning blade and tower vibration from a component-level structural response into a system-level reliability issue. Longer and more flexible blades, taller towers, reduced modal frequencies and platform-induced motions increase blade–tower–support coupling and make vibration prediction more sensitive to modelling assumptions. This review examines blade and tower vibrations in large offshore and floating WTs using a mechanism-informed framework. Six vibration categories are considered: buffeting, periodic and parametric excitation, stall-related self-excited vibration, classical flutter, vortex-induced vibration (VIV), and resonance or modal interaction. For each category, observable vibration signatures are linked to dominant energy pathways, structural degrees of freedom and operating conditions. Modelling approaches are evaluated according to the physical quantities they must capture credibly, including load statistics, phase relationships, time-periodic coefficients, aerodynamic damping, vortex lock-in, modal frequencies and uncertainty bounds. Mitigation strategies are organised by mechanism-specific intervention pathways, including added damping, frequency management, aerodynamic or surface modification, flow-disruption devices, and control or operational measures. Their engineering trade-offs are discussed in terms of power production, load redistribution, offshore accessibility, reliability, maintenance and life-cycle cost are discussed. Future priorities include floating-platform-induced coupling, mechanism-specific validation benchmarks, uncertainty-aware stability and fatigue assessment, digital twins, and life-cycle reliability of mitigation systems. © 2026

Title: A Digital Twin Framework for Proactive Enterprise Management: Research on Operational Decision-making Integrating IoT Data and Computational Modeling
Affiliations: School of Management, Zhengzhou Business University, China
Authors with affiliations: Liu H., School of Management, Zhengzhou Business University, China
Abstract: Digital twin technology provides a powerful computational approach for representing and controlling complex enterprise systems by continuously integrating real-time sensing with dynamic modeling and predictive analytics. The main aim of this study is to develop and demonstrate a reproducible protocol for constructing an IoT-enabled digital twin that enables proactive, data-driven enterprise management. The methodology integrates nonlinear dynamic modeling, observer-based state estimation, uncertainty propagation, risk quantification, and stochastic model predictive control into a unified cyber-physical decision framework. Simulated sensor measurements are assimilated by a state estimator to synchronize the digital twin with the modeled enterprise system, enabling simulation-based prediction of future operational states within a defined computational environment. Uncertainty and risk measures are propagated through the dynamic model to identify emerging instabilities before they escalate into critical failures. A predictive control layer then optimizes multi-objective performance by generating control actions intended to reduce operational risk, stabilize system behavior, and evaluate potential long-term operational efficiency improvements within the simulated scenario. Representative results obtained from a simplified production–inventory–energy simulation model demonstrate the potential advantages of the digital-twin-driven method compared with conventional reactive strategies. The computational example shows smoother operational trajectories, lower cumulative risk, reduced uncertainty, and improved control efficiency across several evaluated performance dimensions. However, these findings are based on a defined simulation workflow and should be interpreted as a proof-of-concept demonstration rather than direct evidence of universal real-world performance. Although the protocol is computational, platform-independent, and potentially adaptable to enterprise domains such as manufacturing, logistics, supply-chain operations, and energy-intensive systems, broader deployment in practical industrial environments would require additional validation using real operational datasets and large-scale implementation studies. By following this procedure, researchers and practitioners can reproduce and further evaluate a scalable, data-driven, and risk-aware digital twin framework for enterprise decision-support applications. © 2026, Journal of Visualized Experiments Journal of Visualized Experiments.

Title: Inverse estimation of directional wave spectrum and response reconstruction using wave buoy analogy
Affiliations: Department of Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering, INHA University, 100, Inha-Ro, Nam-Gu, Incheon, South Korea
Authors with affiliations: Son J., Department of Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering, INHA University, 100, Inha-Ro, Nam-Gu, Incheon, South Korea; Kim Y., Department of Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering, INHA University, 100, Inha-Ro, Nam-Gu, Incheon, South Korea
Abstract: The structural performance of seagoing vessels is influenced by uncertainties arising from material variability, construction tolerances, and stochastic environmental loading. Since long-term operational conditions and fatigue accumulation cannot be fully captured at the design stage, increasing attention has been directed toward operational structural integrity management supported by onboard monitoring and digital twin concepts. Within such frameworks, structural responses at unmeasured locations must be estimated from limited onboard measurements. Directional wave spectrum estimation from ship responses has been widely investigated; however, it remains a fundamentally ill-posed problem due to limited independent information, weak directional sensitivity of response amplitude operators, and numerical instability associated with the nonlinear absolute–encounter frequency conversion under forward-speed conditions. This study extends a non-parametric directional wave spectrum estimation framework to improve robustness under realistic operational conditions. Building on a B-spline surface representation, an adaptive quadrature strategy is introduced to stabilize the absolute–encounter frequency conversion, particularly in regions where multiple absolute frequencies correspond to a single encounter frequency. In addition, a two-stage estimation procedure is employed to improve numerical stability and directional identifiability by separating the identification of energetically relevant regions from subsequent refinement. The proposed framework is validated using 64 full-scale measurement events obtained from an operational container vessel, and the estimated significant wave heights showed strong agreement with ERA5 reanalysis data, while reconstructed response spectral moments exhibited strong linear correlation with the measured responses, with correlation coefficients of approximately 0.93. The results indicate the applicability of the proposed framework under realistic operational conditions, although the estimation performance becomes more sensitive in low sea-state conditions due to the reduced signal-to-noise ratio of measured responses. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Abstract: High-level multilevel inverters, such as the 71-level hybrid cascaded H-bridge topology, can provide high waveform quality, but their design and optimization require time-consuming switching-level simulations. This paper proposes a simulation-driven digital twin framework based on XGBoost for fast virtual measurement of key inverter performance indicators. A MATLAB/Simulink dataset with 700 valid operating points was generated by varying the modulation index, load resistance, and PWM strategy. The trained model estimates total harmonic distortion and inverter power loss with R2 values above 0.9999 on validation and test data, while switching-event information is used as an additional operating indicator in the optimization layer. The corrected prediction and residual analyses show close agreement between the digital-twin estimates and the simulation reference values. The surrogate model reduces the inference time to 0.0437 ms per sample, corresponding to a speedup of approximately 686,430 times compared with a 30 s high-fidelity simulation, with a memory footprint of 318.23 KB. A noise-sensitivity test also shows that the model is highly accurate under nominal conditions but sensitive to perturbed sensor-related inputs, indicating the need for filtering or uncertainty-aware preprocessing before practical sensor-based deployment. Finally, the digital twin is used for Pareto-based operating-point selection, showing how harmonic distortion, switching activity, and power loss can be traded off for application-specific control decisions. The proposed framework therefore provides a fast soft-sensing and optimization layer for simulation-based monitoring and design of high-level multilevel inverters. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Abstract: The accelerated transition toward renewable energy, sustainable infrastructure, and circular economies is driving adoption of advanced materials, including bio-based composites, recycled polymers, nanostructured coatings, and hydrogen-resistant alloys. While critical for net-zero goals, these materials often exhibit heterogeneous architectures, interface-controlled transport, and evolving degradation pathways that complicate reliability, safety, and certifiable long-term performance. Conventional micro- and nano-scale characterization provides indispensable mechanistic insight but frequently relies on destructive sampling and limited coverage, restricting applicability to in-service assets. Nondestructive testing (NDT) therefore provides a complementary life-cycle evidence layer for characterization, monitoring, and qualification under realistic operating conditions. Advances in ultrasonics, eddy currents, infrared thermography, X-ray computed tomography, and optical-fiber sensing enable in situ and real-time assessment across composites, metals, and multifunctional coatings. Combined with artificial intelligence, multimodal sensor fusion, and digital-twin frameworks, NDT is moving beyond diagnostic defect detection toward predictive state estimation that informs design, manufacturing control, maintenance planning, and circular reuse decisions. This Review synthesizes progress across sustainable composites, battery and hydrogen storage systems, smart and self-healing polymers, and nanomaterial-enabled coatings, and distills evidence requirements for credibility at scale, including calibration transfer, robustness to variability and environmental drift, and uncertainty-aware reporting for reuse certification. We also address the sustainability paradox of inspection by highlighting evidence-efficient workflows that balance confidence against energy, resource, and computational costs. Finally, we outline a roadmap toward Inspection Science as a foundational pillar that aligns materials innovation with scalable, decision-grade characterization across full life cycles. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Tribological and Wear Analysis Using Neural Networks
Affiliations: Department of Mechanical Engineering, University Centre for Research and Development, Chandigarh University, Punjab, Mohali, India
Authors with affiliations: Singh J., Department of Mechanical Engineering, University Centre for Research and Development, Chandigarh University, Punjab, Mohali, India
Abstract: Wear prediction is important in tribology, and it determines the behavior and service life of parts such as cutting tools, bearings, and thermal spray coating. The nonlinear relationships between operational variables, material properties, and environmental factors can make conventional models complex. In this chapter, the techniques of representing neural networks (NNs) in wear are discussed, including feedforward NNs, backpropagation NNs, radial basis function NNs, convolutional NNs, recurrent NNs, and long short-term memory. It includes information collection and preprocessing, feature selection, normalization, and missing and imbalanced data. The model assessment based on statistical measures, sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty assessment is described to provide predictive integrity. The practical uses of case studies are illustrated, and comparisons with empirical and analytical models reveal the benefits of NNs. They include the challenges (data quality and the ability to interpret it and integrate it with digital twins), the discussion of the challenges, and the perspectives of reinforcement learning and self-adaptation systems in the future. This chapter offers an extensive predictive wear analysis framework to current tribological systems. © 2027 selection and editorial matter, Jashanpreet Singh and Hitesh Vasudev; individual chapters, the contributors.

Title: Reliability-aware vibration measurement framework for predictive maintenance of rotating machinery: Probability of detection, uncertainty-quantified remaining useful life, and simulator-based hardware-in-the-loop reliability evaluation
Source title: Measurement: Journal of the International Measurement Confederation
Affiliations: Department of Electrical Engineering, Yanbu Industrial College, Yanbu, Saudi Arabia
Authors with affiliations: Sayghe A., Department of Electrical Engineering, Yanbu Industrial College, Yanbu, Saudi Arabia
Abstract: Vibration-based predictive maintenance (PdM) of rotating machinery is increasingly informed by data-driven models, yet two measurement-system limitations restrict deployment in safety-relevant industrial settings: classification accuracy on benchmark data does not characterise the conditional probability of detecting a fault at a given severity along an instrumented measurement chain, and remaining-useful-life (RUL) point estimates do not quantify the uncertainty that risk-informed scheduling requires. This paper develops a reliability-oriented measurement framework that formalises uncertainty propagation from sensor noise and bearing-geometry tolerance through to the inference outputs, and reports three metrological indicators that conventional accuracy-only evaluation does not deliver. The framework combines (i) a Wasserstein conditional GAN with gradient penalty (WCGAN-GP), conditioned on fault label and operating regime, whose synthetic vibration signals are screened by a narrowband signal-to-noise physics-consistency score derived from bearing characteristic frequencies; (ii) a hybrid digital shadow at the edge that fuses a lumped-parameter bearing model with an LSTM-autoencoder anomaly score through a Kalman filter, with Monte Carlo Dropout (pd=0.10, M=100 stochastic forward passes) providing calibrated predictive intervals on RUL; and (iii) a severity-stratified probability-of-detection (PoD) protocol implemented on a simulator-based hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testbed with controlled fault injection (n=300 trials per fault × severity cell). The framework is evaluated on CWRU for imbalanced bearing-fault classification (with bearing-wise cross-validation to prevent window-overlap leakage), on the four C-MAPSS sub-datasets for RUL uncertainty calibration, and on the simulator-based HIL testbed for severity-resolved PoD. Augmentation raises minority-class macro-F1 from 0.71±0.05 to 0.95±0.02 (p<0.001, paired Wilcoxon, five random seeds, Holm–Bonferroni-corrected); the 90% RUL prediction interval achieves empirical coverage 88.4–91.2% on FD001–FD004; HIL PoD exceeds 95% for inner-race, outer-race and ball faults at severity Level 2 and above, falling to 68–79% at incipient severity. End-to-end edge latency on NVIDIA Jetson Orin remains below 85 ms at the 95th percentile, including uncertainty quantification. The results support simulated-HIL reliability evaluation for single bearing faults under controlled severity and stress conditions; field PoD stability for naturally degraded bearings and compound faults remains future work. The contribution is positioned as a reliability-oriented vibration measurement methodology rather than as an AI classifier: uncertainty is propagated from accelerometer noise and bearing-geometry tolerance through to the reported indicators; sensor calibration is traceable under ISO/IEC 17025; severity and PoD are calibrated against the broadband noise floor estimated from a 30-minute baseline acquisition; and every reported headline figure is paired with a confidence interval. The AI components are the means by which the measurement-system indicators are produced, not the contribution itself. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Forecasting-to-scheduling in virtual power plants: Optimization methods, EV/V2G integration, and demand-response orchestration — A strategic review

Abstract: The rapid growth of variable renewable generation and electrified end uses is reshaping power-system operations and amplifying uncertainty across distribution-level portfolios. Virtual power plants (VPPs) address these challenges by coordinating distributed energy resources (DERs), storage, electric vehicles (EVs), and flexible demand to deliver market-facing energy and ancillary services. This review focuses on the methods that determine VPP performance forecasting, optimization, EV integration, and demand-response (DR) orchestration and maps these methods to service requirements and measurable outcomes (e.g., accuracy, latency, feasibility, robustness, and revenue). We first synthesize forecasting approaches for VPP decision support, covering load/renewable/price prediction using modern deep and hybrid models (e.g., N-HiTS, CNN–BiLSTM, KAN) alongside probabilistic and risk-aware forecasting. Particular attention is given to uncertainty representation (e.g., mixture-density models and recurrent probabilistic variants) and to practical trade-offs among data availability, compute budgets, and real-time latency. We then review optimization and scheduling frameworks, ranging from deterministic dispatch to stochastic and robust formulations, receding-horizon/model-predictive control, and two-stage day-ahead/real-time coordination. Scalability is addressed via decomposition and dual/Lagrangian methods for large, heterogeneous portfolios. Next, we examine DR and flexibility-market participation, including program targeting, baseline construction, and settlement, and provide a method-to-service mapping that links algorithm classes to products such as energy, reserves, fast frequency response, and Volt/VAR support. EV integration is treated as a central flexibility lever through V2G/G2V coordination, mobility-aware fleet modeling, charging-network constraints, and degradation-aware scheduling. Finally, we outline the cyber–data stack needed to deploy these methods (IoT/edge–cloud pipelines, streaming analytics, standardized telemetry/APIs, and cybersecurity), and propose benchmarking guidance and a comparative selection matrix. We conclude with open research directions including digital twins, degradation-aware valuation, multi-agent coordination, and trusted settlement mechanisms for emerging flexibility trading. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Consumer-Facing Low-Altitude Urban Air Mobility: Energy-Constrained Service Commitment and Trustworthy Access
Affiliations: Southeast University, School of Electrical Engineering, Nanjing, 210000, China; University of Macau, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, 999078, Macao
Authors with affiliations: Yue J., Southeast University, School of Electrical Engineering, Nanjing, 210000, China; Qian T., Southeast University, School of Electrical Engineering, Nanjing, 210000, China; Hu Q., Southeast University, School of Electrical Engineering, Nanjing, 210000, China; Hui H., University of Macau, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, 999078, Macao
Abstract: Low-altitude urban air mobility (UAM) is moving toward consumer-facing deployment through electrically powered aircraft, digital platforms, and connected vertiport systems. Yet the central challenge is no longer only whether such systems can fly or be scheduled, but whether they can be offered, maintained, and accessed as credible consumer services through digital platforms and connected infrastructure. This review argues that low-altitude UAM for consumers is best understood not as a vehicle-availability problem, but as a commitment-credibility problem bounded by operational supportability and interface continuity. From this perspective, the key analytical object is the service commitment: a platform-issued, operationally informed promise that a passenger request can be incorporated into a supportable near-term service sequence. First, it offers a compact quantitative synthesis showing that consumer-facing UAM service credibility is shaped by passenger-side safety, noise, trust, and service-quality concerns, time–cost sensitivity, and charging readiness. Second, it analyzes how charging availability, battery state, turnaround energy recovery, and power-constrained dispatch determine whether those commitments remain operationally supportable across booking, departure, and execution. Third, it discusses how operational supportability must be translated into passenger-visible service-state updates, uncertainty communication, disruption handling, privacy-conscious data handling, and secure digital access. The review further outlines future research directions in cross-layer service metrics, service-oriented digital twins, interaction-aware recovery, and energy- and trust-aware service design. Overall, it reorganizes UAM- and eVTOL-specific work on operations, vertiport systems, charging readiness, passenger acceptance, and service reliability, while using adjacent-domain studies only as bounded analogies for interface-level mechanisms such as booking updates, recovery communication, and secure access. © 1975-2011 IEEE.

Abstract: The modern equipment development cycle is short, and health service requirements are high; and traditional design methods can no longer meet the needs of equipment development, especially the changes in the health service status of equipment, performance degradation, and the impact of external interference and uncertainty. In order to solve the above problems, this paper focuses on equipment health service and proposes a digital twin-based equipment health service framework, which aims to efficiently use the whole life cycle data to achieve rapid iteration. In order to accurately detect the equipment’s current status in real time, the framework can update the digital twin with operating condition data at various times over the equipment’s whole service life cycle. This digital twin-based approach not only simulates the service status of equipment in the model, but also enables real-time assessment of the health status of the equipment. Through this method, it is possible to better meet the needs of the development and service of modern equipment. To demonstrate the efficacy and viability of the suggested approach, this study uses the permanent magnet synchronous motor, a widely used electromechanical drive device in the aerospace industry, as an example. Abstract: This research presents an integrated framework for energy and sustainability optimization in food production systems, which is based on a combination of digital twin simulation, multi-objective fuzzy optimization, and an Agentic AI layer for contextual selection of operational decisions based on Pareto solutions. The framework evaluates the trade-off between energy consumption, operating cost, carbon emissions, and product quality under operational uncertainty. The empirical analysis of the research is based on data from an industrial food production line and is complemented by digital twin-based simulations to cover a wider range of operating conditions and decision-making scenarios. The results show that the proposed approach reduces energy consumption by about 6–8% and carbon emissions by about 5%, while maintaining product quality stability. These findings indicate that the proposed framework can support more reliable and implementable energy and sustainability decisions in complex food production environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag France SAS, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Abstract: Background: Essential oils (EOs) have emerged as promising natural alternatives to synthetic food preservatives owing to their broad-spectrum antimicrobial, antioxidant, antifungal, and antibiofilm activities. However, their practical application in food systems remains limited by high volatility, oxidative instability, hydrophobicity, uncontrolled release behavior, and inconsistent performance within complex food matrices. Scope and approach: This review introduced a reprogramming paradigm for EO valorization through the integration of programmable delivery architectures, process intensification (PI), artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled sensing, and multi-omics technologies. Unlike previous reviews that primarily address extraction, antimicrobial activity, or encapsulation independently, this work adopts a systems-level perspective that links molecular mechanisms, advanced materials, intensified processing, computational intelligence, and translational implementation within a unified framework for adaptive food preservation. Key findings and conclusions: Recent advances in nanostructured and stimuli-responsive delivery systems, including nanoemulsions, nanostructured lipid carriers, electrospun nanofibers, mesoporous nanomaterials, and biohybrid carriers, have enhanced EO stability, encapsulation efficiency, and controlled-release performance. PI technologies offer opportunities to improve extraction efficiency, sustainability, and manufacturing scalability, whereas AI, machine learning, IoT-enabled sensing, image-based food quality assessment, digital twins, and multi-omics analytics provide powerful tools for predictive optimization, real-time monitoring, and mechanistic elucidation of EO–food–microbe interactions. Nevertheless, significant challenges persist, including limited scalability, food matrix complexity, sensory constraints, fragmented datasets, poor interoperability, regulatory uncertainty, and insufficient industrial validation. This review identifies interconnected scientific, engineering, and digital bottlenecks and proposes a comprehensive gap–solution framework and strategic research roadmap. A conceptual foundation for intelligent, closed-loop EO preservation systems capable of adaptive and predictive functionality is presented. Collectively, this review advances EO research beyond conventional preservation approaches toward scalable, sustainable, and digitally integrated food preservation systems aligned with next-generation industrial and circular bioeconomy objectives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Accounting for approximation errors using surrogate-based parameter estimation of cardiac mechanics digital twins
Source title: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine

Abstract: Background and Objective: Parameter estimation for complex physics-based cardiac models is computationally demanding. Surrogate models can be used to speed up model evaluations and improve the feasibility of estimation and uncertainty quantification. However, the use of surrogates introduces additional sources of error that, if neglected, can cause bias or overconfidence in inferences. Here, we present a general approach to account for such model errors when carrying out surrogate-based parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification. Methods: We use the Bayesian approximation error approach to develop a general framework that systematically accounts for modelling errors and uncertainties induced from the use of a surrogate model. We detail and implement this approach for the task of estimating cardiac stiffness from in-silico 3D left ventricle passive deformation data. We use a finite element model of cardiac mechanics with a neural network-based surrogate, and compare the results with those obtained from a simple regression approach. Results: We show that, despite the sophistication of the neural network, neglecting model errors in the estimation stage leads to biased and overconfident estimates. We demonstrate that our proposed framework allows for simple model-error corrections that provide substantially better inferences. We also demonstrate that our approach can decrease the required number of forward simulations and computational cost for training a neural network by augmenting a low-complexity neural network with a Bayesian approximation error model. Conclusions: We have developed a framework for augmenting surrogate models that improves inference and decreases training time. This has potential for use in the clinical estimation of cardiac stiffness as a biomarker of disease, where efficiency is required at the point of care. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: An adaptive digital twin framework for flow shop scheduling and production planning with machine learning integration

Abstract: Demand fluctuations, machine downtime, and execution plans’ uncertainties affect production planning and scheduling in flow shops; therefore, these factors must be considered during planning to prevent operational disruptions. Unlike existing static integrated planning and scheduling models or heuristic-based dynamic approaches, this work introduces a closed-loop Digital Twin (DT) framework that preserves the mathematical optimality of a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) model while enabling real-time adaptability. Our primary innovation is the systematic and real-time integration of Support Vector Machine (SVM)-based demand forecasting and Association Rule Mining (ARM)-based proactive downtime prediction. We develop a data-driven DT that synchronises the MINLP with live shop-floor data. The framework integrates SVM for demand forecasting and ARM for proactive machine downtime prediction. Through event-driven re-optimisation, the DT continuously updates key parameters and triggers schedule revisions in response to operational deviations. Computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach reduces total operational costs by 13%, significantly decreases machine waiting times and unscheduled downtime, and improves schedule stability compared to static and data-driven baselines. The results underscore the unique value of closed-loop adaptive systems in enhancing resilience and efficiency. This study bridges the gap between traditional optimisation models and real-world execution to offer more responsive and robust production systems. © 2026 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

Title: A design-stage surrogate-assisted optimization framework for ship structural vibration reduction using reduced-order and Bayesian calibration models

Abstract: Design-stage vibration optimization of ship hull structures is often limited by expensive high-fidelity simulations, manual parameter adjustment, and weak closed-loop model updating. To address these issues, this study proposes a Design-stage Surrogate-Assisted Optimization Framework (DSOF). The DSOF integrates automated simulation, data-driven surrogate modeling, uncertainty-aware optimization, and iterative updates to enhance prediction accuracy and optimize performance. First, an automated simulation platform was developed to automatically solve vibration responses under varying parameters, enabling seamless integration between optimization and model updates. Then, a data-driven surrogate modeling approach was employed, combining a Reduced-Order Model (ROM) with Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) calibration, enabling the surrogate model to accurately predict vibration responses and provide uncertainty estimates. Subsequently, the uncertainty information was incorporated into the optimization objectives via a normalized Upper Confidence Bound (UCB), guiding the search toward informative design regions for rapid convergence. Finally, a knee-point-driven multi-objective optimization algorithm was used to achieve a balanced trade-off between vibration suppression and lightweight design. Ablation experiments on a laboratory-scale double-bottom model verified the effectiveness of the main components of the proposed framework. The DSOF variant that integrates both uncertainty awareness and the knee-point strategy (UK-DSOF) demonstrated the highest optimization efficiency and the best vibration-reduction performance among the evaluated methods. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid methodology to combat endemic time and cost overruns in construction, particularly in emerging markets. The study fills a critical gap by integrating three advanced techniques into a single, coherent framework. First, the project schedule is determined by a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model that elastically optimizes time and costs, moving beyond simplistic linear models to account for realistic, nonlinear costs and diminishing returns associated with accelerating project activities. Second, this optimized schedule is rigorously validated through Monte Carlo simulation, which models and quantifies the probabilistic risk of meeting contractual deadlines under real-world uncertainty, transforming a deterministic plan into a risk-informed one with quantifiable confidence levels. Finally, this combined optimization-simulation engine is integrated into a digital twin (DT) platform, which operates as a dynamic system by integrating real-time field data to enable dynamic replanning when conditions change and, importantly, to generate a traceable, data-rich audit trail. This approach, applied to a Moroccan real estate project, provides more realistic cost-time tradeoffs than traditional assumptions, and becomes legally defensible and invaluable for supporting claims, justifying resource allocation, and strengthening a party's position in contractual disputes.  © 2026 This work is made available under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license,.

Abstract: System discovery, such as parameter estimation or model reconstruction, in complex power system assets can play crucial roles in condition monitoring, troubleshooting and root cause analysis. However, robust system discovery in presence of noisy or sparse data is a challenging problem that requires solving an inverse problem and quantifying uncertainties. In this paper we address this problem and propose an approach to find the solution by using Physics-Informed Machine Learning approach for modeling cause and effect in power systems assets with polynomial dynamics. In a probabilistic setting we establish the merits of the proposed approach using empirical results. In particular, we benchmark our proposed end-to-end method with a baseline that uses Bayesian Neural Network with dropout and show that our approach outperforms baseline by 79% of reduction of validation error, 34% reduction of training time and 97.5% reduction of inference time. © 2026

Title: Bridging the gap: towards a digital twin to optimize therapeutic cell-seeding strategies in nerve tissue engineering

Abstract: Abstract – Peripheral nerve injuries impose a substantial strain on the lives of millions of people worldwide. Engineered neural tissues provide a promising avenue to improve peripheral nerve repair strategies, potentially allowing the precise seeding of cells and materials that support regenerative processes. Current optimization of cell-seeding strategies relies on testing the impact of relevant parameters in vivo, requiring considerable time and resources. We propose an alternative approach to the design of cellular hydrogels based on a mathematical cell–solute model, informed via in vitro experiment, to identify promising cell-seeding strategies in silico at a limited cost. These designs are manufactured using 3D-printed moulds and validated in vivo. We evaluate the regenerative potential of these designs by focusing on the impact of different cell-seeding strategies on vascular endothelial growth factor secretion and gradient generation, both crucial elements of regenerative angiogenesis in early nerve repair. In this way, we provide a first proof-of-concept of a digital twin for nerve tissue engineering, which uses in silico, in vitro and in vivo repair models. © 2026 The Authors.

Abstract: Hydropower governor seals face persistent micro-leakage risks under non-stationary frequency regulation loads. This work establishes a calibratable multiscale framework to predict such leakage by mapping online signals - differential pressure, temperature, and assembly time - to nominal contact pressure. Interfacial connectivity is quantified via the real contact area fraction and critical constriction height, with the leakage rate and its uncertainty derived from a cubic-law formulation. To ensure engineering viability, the model is reduced to two key parameters: topographic concentration and channel modifier, which can be identified from one-off topography measurement and sparse early-stage leakage observations. Case studies reveal that viscoelastic relaxation coupled with surface degradation can trigger percolation-driven leakage. Within 0.05-0.2 Hz, leakage is dominated by pressure amplitude and temperature-dependent viscosity rather than excitation frequency. The framework links micro-scale tribology to macro-scale operation data and provides a calibratable and deployable physics-based submodel for digital twins and predictive maintenance of hydropower systems.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Research on the Autonomous Decision System of Nuclear Power Plant Accident Operation Procedure Based on Digital Twin and Hybrid Intelligence
Source title: 8th Asia Energy and Electrical Engineering Symposium, AEEES 2026

Abstract: To address the limitations of traditional nuclear power plant accident operation procedures in dynamic adaptability, proactive early warning, and intelligent decision-making, this study proposes an autonomous decision-making accident operation management system. The system integrates digital twin and hybrid intelligence technologies to establish a real-time synchronized digital twin model with physical power plants. By combining high-fidelity physical models with data-driven simulations, it achieves dynamic prediction of accident progression and quantification of uncertainties. Building on this foundation, the system designs a state-oriented autonomous execution engine that utilizes state-action mapping mechanisms to drive dynamic execution and transitions of digital procedures. A unified data bus is established to integrate the entire technical chain from data perception, model computation to human-machine collaboration. Case analysis demonstrates that the system reduces diagnosis time for typical accidents by approximately 60% and secures over 15% more decision-making time windows for critical operations through proactive prediction, significantly enhancing the timeliness and accuracy of accident response. This system achieves a paradigm shift from "passive response"to "proactive early warning and autonomous decision-making,"providing theoretical foundations and engineering feasible pathways for intelligent safety operations in nuclear power plants.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Non-uniform indoor environments have emerged as a promising paradigm for improving energy efficiency, indoor air quality, and occupant-centric comfort in buildings. Non-uniform indoor environments refer to the deliberate creation of spatially or locally differentiated environmental parameters to meet diverse comfort and health needs while reducing overall energy consumption. This review presents a comprehensive and integrated analysis of the development of non-uniform indoor environments from three interrelated perspectives: sensing, prediction, and ventilation. First, advances in environmental sensing technologies are systematically summarized, including fixed sensor networks, mobile sensing platforms, and multimodal recognition systems. Second, state-of-the-art prediction methods for indoor environmental fields are reviewed, covering physically simplified computational fluid dynamics approaches, reduced-order models, and emerging data-driven techniques, highlighting the transition toward real-time and high-efficiency prediction. Third, ventilation systems for creating non-uniform environments are analyzed across multiple spatial scales, ranging from space-divided ventilation systems to personalized and wearable microenvironmental systems, demonstrating a clear evolution toward occupant-centric and demand-oriented control. Based on the reviewed literature, key challenges are identified in sensor deployment optimization, multimodal data fusion, model generalization and uncertainty quantification, and the stability and coordination of multi-scale airflow organization. Future research directions are proposed, including the integration of sensing, prediction, and control within closed-loop frameworks, the development of digital twin-enabled intelligent systems, and the establishment of evaluation metrics tailored to non-uniform environments. The findings highlight the technological convergence required for future intelligent and occupant-centric indoor environmental control systems. © 2026

Title: Digital twin use-case prioritisation for sustainability in smart manufacturing: A multi-criteria decision analytics approach

Abstract: Manufacturers face growing pressure to invest in digital twins for sustainability and supply chain resilience. Yet, no systematic framework exists to guide the prioritisation of use cases amid competing objectives and practical resource constraints. Digital twins, which integrate real-time sensing, simulation, big data analytics, and artificial intelligence, are among the frontier technologies reshaping industrial production, and their prioritisation is a core socio-economic planning problem of the Industry 4.0 transition. This study addresses this gap by developing an interview-informed multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) that prioritises seven recurring digital twin use cases based on sustainability and operational benefits, as well as implementation and scaling burdens. The decision model scores sustainability benefits and feasibility burdens directly. At the same time, implications for supply chain resilience are interpreted ex post through the comparative positioning of the use cases rather than being scored as a separate family of criteria. Drawing on 50 semi-structured expert interviews conducted across 27 countries, the analysis combines qualitative content analysis with a pipeline comprising TOPSIS, VIKOR, and Stochastic Multicriteria Acceptability Analysis (SMAA). Criteria weights derived from interview salience reveal that data readiness, legacy integration, and interoperability effort dominate the prioritisation. The energy and facilities twin ranks first in TOPSIS. In contrast, the supply chain and scenario twin emerge as the VIKOR compromise solution and the most robust first-rank option under interview-centred weight uncertainty (85.6% probability). Sensitivity analysis shows that product passport and circularity twins rise to the top when sustainability benefits are privileged over feasibility burdens. The results yield a prioritisation framework for digital twin investment applicable to manufacturers, industry consortia, and policymakers designing Industry 4.0 roadmaps. Prescriptive implications address both private-sector technology prioritisation and staged implementation, and public policy on digital infrastructure, interoperability standards, and sustainability regulation, with attention to emerging economies. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Metaheuristic optimization of laminated composite structures: methods, trends, and future directions

Abstract: Laminated composite structures are widely used in aerospace, automotive, marine, and civil engineering due to their high strength-to-weight ratio, tailorability, and durability. However, their anisotropic nature, multiple interacting failure modes, and multi-physics loading conditions make optimal design a high-dimensional, nonlinear, and multi-objective challenge. Conventional gradient-based optimization often struggles in such complex design spaces, prompting the growing use of metaheuristic algorithms. This review goes beyond conventional algorithm-centric surveys by introducing a framework-level synthesis of metaheuristic optimization in laminated composites, explicitly integrating physics-informed modeling, uncertainty-aware design, and digital twin-enabled optimization paradigms, which are largely absent in existing reviews. Key trends identified include the superiority of hybrid and surrogate-assisted approaches in reducing computational cost, the role of adaptive operators in preventing premature convergence, and the potential of physics-informed and uncertainty-aware metaheuristics for real-world implementation. This work provides researchers and engineers with a comprehensive and comparative reference to guide the selection and development of metaheuristic algorithms. By synthesizing two decades of algorithmic progress, this review not only provides a comparative landscape but also codifies the fundamental challenges, such as the combinatorial curse and the simulation-to-reality gap, that define the current frontier, thereby establishing a clear roadmap for the next generation optimization frameworks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Agentic Control Towers: Multi Agent LLM RL Orchestration for Autonomous and Resilient Supply Chains
Source title: Accelerating Logistics Through Generative AI, Digital Twins, and Autonomous Operations
Affiliations: University of Bisha, Saudi Arabia
Authors with affiliations: Awad A., University of Bisha, Saudi Arabia; Alahmari D., University of Bisha, Saudi Arabia
Abstract: Supply chains exist today under chronic volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity. Batch based planning and decision rights fragmentation render companies sluggish to detect disruption and costly to rebound. This paper develops an integrated concept—Agentic Control Towers (ACTs)which combines large language model (LLM) agents, multi agent reinforcement learning (MARL), and digital supply chain twins to provide closed loop, explainable autonomy for plan, source, make, move, and serve. We integrate findings across inventory and logistics reinforcement learning, LLM tooling and multiagent coordination, digital twin orchestration, and resilient operations. We position ACTs as a decision fabric that continuously senses, simulates, negotiates, and performs while placing guardrails for safety, sustainability, cost, and service. The paper provides an integrated architecture, end to end decision flows, stability and governance design decisions, and evidence informed pathways of impact. We also establish evaluation criteria. Title: Digital twin framework for structural health monitoring using PWT-excited Lamb waves
Source title: Mechanics of Advanced Materials and Structures
Affiliations: Department of Aerospace Engineering, Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Kerala, Trivandrum, India
Authors with affiliations: Harikumar V., Department of Aerospace Engineering, Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Kerala, Trivandrum, India; Bijudas C.R., Department of Aerospace Engineering, Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Kerala, Trivandrum, India
Abstract: Non-destructive structural health monitoring (SHM) employs techniques that allow for the continuous evaluation of structural integrity without causing harm to the structure itself. By utilising methods such as Lamb wave propagation and detection using piezoelectric wafer transducer (PWT), these systems enable the early detection of defects or damage, ensuring the safety and longevity of critical infrastructure. PWTs are employed to generate and detect guided waves, such as Lamb waves (LW), within the structures. These waves propagate through the structure, and the responses can be analysed to identify the presence of damage. Nonetheless, damage identification via damage-sensitive features derived from diverse signal processing techniques may prove ineffective in real-world settings characterised by several uncertainties. To address these challenges, a digital twin model that accommodates these uncertainties in SHM using PWAS is presented. The bonding between the sensor and the structure can significantly impact SHM applications where partial contact loss may lead to incorrect conclusions, potentially being misinterpreted as damage within the structure. A data-driven approach is implemented to develop a digital twin (DT) model that distinguishes between healthy and damaged states. Experimental studies are conducted with a wafer-type sensor coupled to an elastic plate, and a laser vibrometer is used as a receiver to analyse the A0 mode behaviour at different points within a 30 cm radius surrounding the sensor. Mode tuning curves for a frequency range from 13 kHz to 260 kHz are obtained, with the amplitude found to vary with bonding conditions. The obtained response is then used to train the digital twin model, which can be further tested with damage scenarios. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, N V R Naidu, K R V Subramanian, Nagaraju Kottam and G N Anil Kumar, individual chapters, the contributors.

Abstract: Dualistic production and intralogistics (DPiL) have inherently intricate spatio-temporal coupling relationships. Meanwhile, the occurrence of disturbance propagation further amplifies such complexity, aggravating operation control difficulty. This novel problem is summarized as the dualistic production and intralogistics synchronized control problem (DPiLSynC) considering disturbance propagation. Traditional production planning and control (PPC) methods overlook the impact of disturbance propagation, significantly compromising system stability. Fortunately, digital twin (DT) technology promises rapid identification of disturbances by physical-virtual interaction. The adverse effects of disturbances may diffuse across the manufacturing system, causing operational disruptions. But analyzing the spatio-temporal characteristics of disturbance propagation is challenging due to the unclear connection-interaction mechanism of multiple DT models in manufacturing systems. This paper proposes a temporal-digital twin-network (T-DT-N) enabled Out-of-Order (OoO) synchronized control approach. Firstly, the modified OoO framework with disturbance propagation analysis is designed to reconstruct the operation logic of DPiL. Secondly, T-DT-N is developed to reveal the spatio-temporal evolution patterns of disturbance propagation by introducing the temporal network to model connection-interaction relationships of DT models. Thirdly, OoO synchronized control using propagation analysis results is proposed, involving three distinct control phases, each considering multiple factors aiming to achieve resilient DPiL operation. Computation results indicate this approach achieves shorter order makespan, shopfloor throughput time, and waiting time, while decreasing the percentage tardy. Furthermore, it exhibits stability across varying queue lengths and uncertain levels, thereby validating its application in a dynamic environment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Abstract: The accurate estimation of the energy consumption of an Electric Vehicle (EV) under variable conditions, such as topography, traffic, and road characteristics, is essential for predicting range, planning trips, and ensuring operational safety. However, the uncertainty associated with the real battery behavior remains one of the major concerns for EV users, motivating the development of tools capable of representing and anticipating this consumption more reliably. In this context, this work proposes a Digital Twin (DT) architecture dedicated to energy monitoring and decision-support for Intelligent and Connected EVs (ICEVs). The system integrates the SUMO (Simulation of Urban MObility) traffic simulator with an external energy model, employing the A∗ algorithm for initial route planning, in which the selected route corresponds to the one with the lowest estimated energy consumption. Elevation data obtained through the Google Elevation Application Programming Interface (API) are also incorporated into the route topology to compute road gradients and their impact on energy consumption. The validation considers data from a simulated EV, where the DT continuously compares the estimated consumption with the observed one during the simulation, identifying deviations greater than 15% and applying autonomous decision rules based on critical (20%) and safety (10%) battery levels. When necessary, the system performs dynamic route re-planning or redirects the vehicle to a charging point. The results demonstrate that the DT identifies consumption anomalies, adapts to operational variations, and guarantee a safe autonomy margin for the vehicle. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Transitioning to resilient, renewable, and EV-integrated power systems demands computational frameworks capable of handling high uncertainty, distributed decision-making, and large-scale dynamics. Classical AI and optimisation struggle with high-dimensional interactions among generators, storage, EV fleets, and real-time grid states. This paper proposes a quantum-AI smart grid architecture combining quantum machine learning, quantum-inspired combinatorial optimisation, and hybrid quantum-classical control. Grid states are encoded in variational quantum circuits and Quadratic unconstrained binary optimisation models, accelerating dispatch, scheduling, congestion management, and optimal power flow. A layered design integrates edge-level classical controllers with cloud-based quantum solvers for utility-compatible deployment. Evaluations on a high-fidelity quantum-assisted digital twin of a renewable- and EV-rich IEEE 14-bus network show 40-60% faster optimisation, improved stability, and enhanced solution robustness over classical baselines, demonstrating quantum-AI as a transformative enabler for next-generation power systems.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Scan-to-engineering: From reality capture to digital models in civil engineering
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China; Key Laboratory of Civil Engineering Safety and Durability of China Ministry of Education, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China
Authors with affiliations: Li J.-F., Department of Civil Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China; Liu Y.-F., Department of Civil Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China, Key Laboratory of Civil Engineering Safety and Durability of China Ministry of Education, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China; Fan J.-S., Department of Civil Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China, Key Laboratory of Civil Engineering Safety and Durability of China Ministry of Education, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China
Abstract: Reality capture technologies, including terrestrial laser scanning, mobile laser scanning, and UAV-based sensing, offer non-contact means to document civil infrastructure. The ultimate goal of Scan-to-Engineering is to convert dense point clouds into engineering-usable models for measurement, information management, simulation, and decision support. Drawing on 123 core studies, this review examines recent advances in acquisition, point cloud processing, model generation, and downstream applications across civil infrastructure. The reviewed work is organized into three task-specific outputs: Scan-to-Geometry, Scan-to-BIM, and Scan-to-FEM. Engineering Model Readiness Levels and Validation Maturity are used to relate model content to evidence strength. Current studies show substantial progress in geometry-ready, information-ready, and selected analysis-ready workflows, but decision-ready applications remain limited. The review concludes by identifying challenges in observability, automation, uncertainty traceability, interoperability, and updatable digital twins. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V.

Title: Spatial–temporal event compiler: Look-around reasoning for uncertainty-aware synchronization in digital twin-driven manufacturing systems
Affiliations: Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong; Research Institute for Advanced Manufacturing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong; School of Mechanical Engineering, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China; Department of Production Engineering, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden

Abstract: Personalized production is widely adopted in discrete manufacturing due to its ability to meet diverse customer requirements through flexible combinations of components. However, it also poses significant challenges to production synchronization, which requires all necessary operators, tools, materials, and industrial robots to be available within the prescribed time and space. In complex multi-stage manufacturing processes, execution deviations can accumulate into operation-level uncertainty, namely the risk that an operation cannot start, proceed, or finish as scheduled because the required resources and execution conditions are no longer aligned. Such uncertainty undermines resource utilization and may trigger cascading delays across the entire process. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a spatial–temporal event compiler (STEC) framework comprising digital, knowledge, and reasoning engines for compiling and analyzing manufacturing events. Specifically, the state information of digital models is compiled into a spatial–temporal event graph, which is continuously updated through a multi-clock alignment scheme that aligns distinct planning, scheduling, and execution time scales. Within the reasoning engine, a look-around reasoning approach is developed to capture historical consistency, the current execution context, and near-future evolution trends by integrating look-backward, look-present, and look-forward perspectives, thereby enabling uncertainty assessment. Furthermore, an LLM-based synchronization mechanism is incorporated into the framework to provide status reports through multi-turn interactions, allowing managers to query the current execution status and assess potential downstream impacts for timely intervention. Finally, a case study demonstrates that STEC improves the accuracy and stability of uncertainty identification. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Abstract: The rapid growth of renewable generation and electric mobility introduces substantial uncertainty into modern power systems, requiring demand-response (DR) strategies that are both intelligent and physically reliable. This paper proposes DR-DL, a unified deep learning and digital-twin architecture for real-time, adaptive DR in smart grids. Using a high-resolution 100,000-sample operational dataset capturing consumer load, coordinated EV charging, solar/wind profiles, and time-varying prices, DR-DL combines multi-horizon probabilistic forecasting (Temporal Fusion Transformers) with a deep reinforcement learning controller to achieve peak-load mitigation, cost-effective load shifting, and constraint-aware EV charging. A physics-informed digital twin operates in parallel to synchronise grid states, validate control actions, and assess robustness under disturbances. Results show that DR-DL reduces the peak-to-average ratio by up to 27%, increases renewable utilization, and eliminates violations of voltage and operational constraints. DR-DL also exhibits faster, more stable convergence during learning than conventional deep reinforcement learning baselines, yielding sustained cost savings and improved resilience to abrupt load and generation fluctuations. These results demonstrate a scalable, grid-aware DR solution suitable for practical deployment.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The rapid proliferation of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has introduced significant challenges in managing grid load balance and mitigating transformer overloading, particularly in large-scale charging infrastructures. This paper presents a Resilient Grid Overload Mitigation and Slot Efficiency Optimization with Fault-Tolerant Digital Twin Control for Distributed Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (GROMS-FTDTC) algorithm designed to ensure resilient and efficient operation of multiple EV charging systems under dynamic grid conditions. The proposed framework integrates a quantum-enhanced digital twin of the charging network, enabling real-time simulation, predictive control, and fault tolerance. The control strategy incorporates detailed Grid Load and Overload Modeling to capture the temporal and spatial variations in demand, along with a Grid Overload Indicator to detect and quantify transformer stress levels. Additionally, a Slot Utilization Modeling mechanism is developed to optimize the allocation of charging slots across stations, while a Slot Underutilization Penalty is introduced to discourage inefficient resource usage. The decision-making process is formulated as a multi-objective optimization problemthat minimizes a composite cost function consisting of a grid overload penalty and a slot underutilization penalty, ensuring both grid stability and operational efficiency. Simulation results on a multi-station, multi-slot EV charging scenario demonstrate that the GROMS-FTDTC algorithm effectively mitigates grid load imbalance, reduces overload occurrences, and maximizes slot utilization, even under fault and uncertainty conditions. The proposed framework offers a scalable and intelligent control solution for future smart grid-integrated EV charging networks.  © 2025 IEEE.

Abstract: The realization of resilient autonomous systems is currently impeded by the difficulty of translating abstract design requirements into verifiable control policies that can withstand significant model uncertainty. Here we present the Agentic Control Framework, a full-stack neuro-symbolic architecture that unifies semantic reasoning with game-theoretic hardening to maximize robustness. The workflow initiates with a Large Language Model (LLM)-based agent that leverages a domainspecific Knowledge Graph to comprehend unstructured design specifications and retrieve optimal control constraints. These formal specifications characterize a high-fidelity Digital Twin, which incorporates a Reduced Order Model (ROM) integrated via Runge-Kutta (RK4) methods. Within this adaptive environment, we solve the robust control problem as a multi-agent zero-sum differential game using Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), where a stabilizing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy competes against an adversary injecting worst-case stochastic disturbances. We benchmark this adversarial formulation against classical H∞ synthesis and standard Vanilla PPO, demonstrating that the system converges to an empirical Nash Equilibrium that rivals theoretical robust control baselines. Our results indicate that grounding agentic comprehension in rigorous game-theoretic training produces self-organizing controllers that maintain operational stability under severe uncertainty, bridging the gap between theoretical robust control and adaptive autonomy. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A Review of Stope Layout Optimization Algorithms: Linking Resource Efficiency, Circular Mining, and Sustainable Production

Abstract: The optimization of stope layouts is one of the most critical and computationally demanding challenges in underground mine planning, with direct implications for economic performance, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. This review synthesizes the evolution of algorithmic approaches to stope layout optimization—comprising the design of the stope shape and the placement of the stope within the parent orebody, tracing progress from early deterministic heuristics to advanced frameworks based on mathematical programming, network flow formulations, metaheuristics, stochastic optimization, and artificial intelligence. Early fixed-geometry methods provided operational simplicity but were constrained by high dilution, ore loss, and limited adaptability to geological variability. Subsequent developments in variable-size and hybrid optimization algorithms improved geometric conformity to orebodies, leading to enhanced ore recovery and reduced waste extraction. More recent research integrates stope design with production scheduling, explicitly represents geological uncertainty, and incorporates data-driven and digital-twin technologies to support continuous decision making in uncertain conditions. While much of the literature has focused on maximizing economic value under technical constraints, this review highlights the growing convergence between optimization performance and resource-efficiency and circular mining principles supporting sustainable production. Algorithms that effectively control dilution, improve material selectivity, and enhance robustness under uncertainty are shown to simultaneously reduce energy intensity, waste, and tailings generation, thereby improving mineral resource retention and reducing irreversible material losses. The findings emphasize the need for scalable, multi-objective, and uncertainty-aware optimization frameworks that integrate geotechnical stability, economic value, and environmental performance to support resilient, resource-efficient, and circular underground mining operations aligned with sustainable production objectives. © Society for Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration Inc. 2026.

Abstract: This paper uses a bibliometric approach to map the literature on harnessing Digital Twinning concepts, models, and applications in the context of material and structural fatigue. It aims to explore how this topic has developed over time, identify key researchers contributing significantly to the field, and analyze the network connections among researchers in this rapidly growing area of structural mechanics. Additionally, a frequency-based co-occurrence study was conducted to find the most relevant keywords in scientific publications related to Digital Twins in mechanical fatigue. Several keywords were selected as control terms to create a conceptual thematic map, which visualizes the main research trends. The findings reveal broad interdisciplinary effects across various engineering fields by highlighting three interconnected themes: Digital Twinning for uncertainty quantification and optimization, Finite Element Analysis for fatigue life-based design and simulation, and Structural Health Monitoring for damage detection in materials and structures. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Abstract: The growing complexity of, and demand from, modern supply chains, coupled with technological advancements, have enabled the advent of smart warehouses. In these infrastructures, several technological advancements, such as: automation, robotics, simulation, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Internet of Things (IoT) devices; are employed to enhance operational performance. This work details a structured literature review, focused on smart warehouses, uncovering the role of discrete-event simulation (DES) in that domain. Particularly, in the development and optimization of smart warehouses. Moreover, it is explored how data integration, and its structuring, is critical to smart warehouses, and how it all can enable the contribution of simulation, supporting informed decision-making. The review covers key areas, including the historical evolution of warehouse systems, past scientific links between simulation and warehouse systems, the integration of AI on smart warehouses, Digital Twins of smart warehouses, the sustainability of smart warehouses, and the challenges to their implementation, such as high implementation costs, technical integration difficulties, and organization challenges. The findings highlight the strategic value of simulation in supporting the transition to more adaptive, intelligent warehouse systems, testing operational scenarios, and managing uncertainty. This paper concludes by identifying research opportunities that focus on scalable data-driven approaches to simulation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Intelligent Control and System Integration of Process Equipment Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning

Abstract: Industrial process equipment is characterized by strong nonlinearity, multivariable coupling, and dynamic uncertainty, posing significant challenges to traditional control methods. To address these issues, this paper proposes an intelligent control and system integration framework based on deep reinforcement learning. A Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm is adopted and enhanced with safety-constrained reward design to ensure reliable operation under industrial constraints. Additionally, an LSTM-based state encoder is incorporated to capture temporal dependencies and improve control performance in dynamic environments. A digital twin-assisted hybrid learning strategy is further introduced to enable safe and efficient training. The proposed framework integrates control, optimization, and fault diagnosis into a unified closed-loop architecture. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms conventional PID, MPC, and baseline DRL methods in terms of tracking accuracy, energy efficiency, and safety. These findings highlight its potential for practical industrial applications. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: This chapter reviews the evolving technology landscape of industrialized construction (IC) through the integration of automation, robotics, and artificial intelligence (AI). Rather than treating innovations as isolated tools, it adopts a functional, closed-loop view-linking sensing and localization, execution semantics and modeling, decision and optimization, execution and control, and verification and compliance-to explain how task chains can produce computable states, constraint-aware decisions, and auditable outcomes across the factory-logistics-site continuum. It further examines the shift of AI from recognition-oriented applications toward executable decision support, including the emerging roles of generative AI and digital twins as runtime systems for prediction and rolling replanning under uncertainty. Next-generation robotics is synthesized as process-embedded execution units for material handling and assembly, connection and closure, surface finishing, and autonomous construction equipment, alongside construction-scale additive manufacturing. Despite the technological strides, the chapter addresses the challenges these innovations face, including the unpredictable nature of construction sites and the slow integration of AI into established workflows. Looking forward, the text discusses the potential for a transformative impact on IC through the synergy of AI, robotics, and modular construction techniques, which could lead to more sustainable. © 2026 Xiao Li.

Title: Digital twins and artificial intelligence for predictive maintenance in microelectromechanical systems (MEMS): a techno-economic perspective
Affiliations: School of Economics and Management, Jiujiang Polytechnic University of Science and Technology, Jiujiang, China
Authors with affiliations: Zhou T., School of Economics and Management, Jiujiang Polytechnic University of Science and Technology, Jiujiang, China; Hu C., School of Economics and Management, Jiujiang Polytechnic University of Science and Technology, Jiujiang, China; Liu D., School of Economics and Management, Jiujiang Polytechnic University of Science and Technology, Jiujiang, China; Duan Y., School of Economics and Management, Jiujiang Polytechnic University of Science and Technology, Jiujiang, China; Zhang Z., School of Economics and Management, Jiujiang Polytechnic University of Science and Technology, Jiujiang, China
Abstract: This structured narrative review examines when digital twin-enabled predictive maintenance for MEMS is economically and technically defensible. We show that the strongest business case arises only when degradation is observable, sufficient lead time exists for intervention, and the avoided cost of failure exceeds monitoring and integration costs. The review distinguishes digital twins from digital models and simulation frameworks, summarizes MEMS-specific sensing and packaging constraints, and introduces a transparent review protocol, a benchmarking checklist, and a decision matrix for unit-level, fleet-level, screening, and redesign-first strategies. Overall, the literature supports a conditional rather than universal case for MEMS PdM, with value concentrated in high-criticality applications that combine actionable data, calibrated uncertainty, and organizational readiness. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.
