Abstract: Background: Advances in the theory and methods of computational oncology have enabled accurate characterization and prediction of tumor growth and treatment response on a patient-specific basis. This capability can be integrated into a digital twin framework in which bi-directional data-flow between the physical tumor and the digital tumor facilitate dynamic model re-calibration, uncertainty quantification, and clinical decision-support via recommendation of optimal therapeutic interventions. However, many digital twin frameworks rely on bespoke implementations tailored to each disease site, modeling choice, and algorithmic implementation. Results: We present TumorTwin, a modular and differentiable software framework for initializing, updating, and leveraging patient-specific cancer tumor digital twins. TumorTwin is publicly available as a Python package, with associated documentation, datasets, and tutorials. Novel contributions include the development of a patient-data structure adaptable to different disease sites, a modular architecture to enable the composition of different data, model, solver, and optimization objects, and CPU or GPU parallelized implementations of forward model solves and gradient computations. We demonstrate the functionality of TumorTwin via an in silico dataset of high-grade glioma growth and response to radiation therapy. Conclusion: The TumorTwin framework enables rapid prototyping and testing of image-guided oncology digital twins. This allows researchers to systematically investigate different models, algorithms, disease sites, or treatment decisions while leveraging robust numerical and computational infrastructure. © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: This study outlines the development and testing of a Digital Twin Ocean (DTO) framework, aimed at improving coastal ocean forecasts through the use of autonomous underwater gliders. A fleet of gliders were deployed in the western English Channel during August-September 2024 to collect measurements of temperature, salinity, chlorophyll and oxygen, aiming to track the movement of the harmful algal bloom Karenia mikimotoi. Measurements were assimilated into a very high resolution (1.5 km) numerical forecast model, with an implementation of biogeochemistry data assimilation for this purpose. The model forecast was then used by a probabilistic uncertainty model to plan a series of waypoints to navigate the glider fleet towards features of interest. By utilising a continuous feedback loop of measurement, prediction, guidance, and refinement a system with real time coupling between the real ocean environment and its digital counterpart has been established. Building upon a prior pilot study of, this work improves every element of the system to address several limitations of the prior configuration. Whilst a bloom was present in the wider area, measurements and modeling suggest it didn't enter the glider operation zone. Despite this and other operational challenges the mission clearly demonstrates the benefits of such a system. The ability to simultaneously track multiple features of interest, namely chlorophyll maxima and oxygen minima, would not have been possible with a single glider resulting in significant benefits to the system. Furthermore, the improvement to biogeochemical forecasting has been demonstrated through a series of post mission experiments, highlighting the advantages of high temporal resolution observations and increased spatial resolution of the model. © 2026 Dale Partridge et al.

Title: Multidisciplinary coupled dynamics modeling of electro-mechanical actuator considering nonlinear clearances in multiple stages; [考虑多环节间隙非线性的电动舵机多学科耦合动力学建模]

Abstract: Due to uncertainties in the design and assembly process, nonlinear factors such as clearances often exist in multiple sectors of the aerospace electro-mechanical actuator transmission system, significantly affecting the working quality of the electro-mechanical actuator. Therefore, it is essential to accurately establish a nonlinear dynamic model for the electro-mechanical actuator accurately. Moreover, electro-mechanical actuators involve multiple disciplines such as servo control, motor transmission, reduction mechanism, structural elasticity, etc., making the modeling process highly challenging. The research object in this paper is a standard ball screw-type electromechanical actuator. Considering the elastic stiffness of actuator transmission components and the nonlinearity of clearances at gear pairs, supporting bearings, and fork pairs, the motor dynamics and servo controllers are finely modeled. The electro-mechanical actuator system is represented by a high-fidelity multidisciplinary dynamic model that can account for nonlinearities in different sector clearances. Furthermore, simulation analysis of the electromechanical actuator system performance is conducted. The simulation results are compared with ground vibration test results of the actuator-rudder system. The results indicate that the multidisciplinary coupled dynamic model of the electro-mechanical actuator established in this paper can reflect the influence and degree of influence of the clearances in different parts of the mechanism. The simulation and experimental results are in good agreement, with a maximum error of less than 10%. This research lays the foundation for the digital twin study of complex aerospace electric servo systems. Copyright © 2026 Journal of Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics. Title: Data-driven perspectives on pyrolysis of heterogeneous solid waste for hydrogen production: A comprehensive review

Abstract: The rapid accumulation of heterogeneous solid waste has created severe pressures on environmental management and resource recovery. Pyrolysis and pyrolysis–reforming can convert complex solid waste streams into hydrogen-rich gas. They are therefore promising pathways for both waste valorization and low-carbon hydrogen production. However, pyrolysis-based hydrogen production is difficult to describe using conventional mechanistic models. The difficulty is driven by feedstock heterogeneity, complex reaction networks, and multiscale reaction–transport coupling. This review examines machine learning (ML) applications in pyrolysis-based hydrogen production from heterogeneous solid waste from a data-driven perspective. Key topics include H₂-related output prediction, key-variable identification, catalyst screening, and operating-condition optimization. Reactor-level support and system assessment assisted by techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) are also discussed. ML can improve prediction and optimization efficiency under controlled data conditions. Nevertheless, insufficient data quality, inconsistent evaluation standards, limited model generalizability, and weak deployment adaptability still constrain its engineering application. Future efforts should strengthen standardized data infrastructures, physics-informed modelling, and uncertainty quantification. Stronger integration among ML, TEA, LCA, digital twins (DTs), and large language models (LLMs) is also needed. These advances will help move pyrolysis-based hydrogen production from laboratory prediction toward engineering scale-up and system deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Abstract: Tunnel leakage threatens the durability, safety, and serviceability of underground infrastructure, while conventional inspection methods remain limited by low efficiency, subjectivity, and poor capability for hidden seepage assessment. This review aims to clarify recent progress in artificial intelligence-based tunnel leakage detection and monitoring by examining sensing technologies, intelligent interpretation methods, and multimodal fusion strategies from a measurement-oriented perspective. Electromagnetic, optical, mechanical, vibration/acoustic, environmental, wireless, self-powered, and multi-parameter sensing approaches are compared according to their measurable quantities, applicable tasks, advantages, limitations, and uncertainty sources. Deep learning methods are discussed in relation to leakage classification, detection, segmentation, localization, quantification, and early warning. The review indicates that vision- and LiDAR-assisted methods are comparatively mature for visible leakage recognition, boundary segmentation, and spatial localization, whereas fiber-optic, acoustic, thermal, and environmental sensing, supported by wireless and self-powered platforms, is better suited to hidden seepage inference, distributed monitoring, and long-term warning. Practical implementation is still constrained by limited annotated datasets, inconsistent calibration, environmental interference, weak cross-tunnel generalization, and insufficient evaluation of measurement robustness. To address these challenges, the Pluralistic Resonant Perception Theory (PRPT) is introduced as a conceptual framework for organizing heterogeneous sensing information, cross-modal interaction, spatiotemporal coordination, and semantic-mechanistic coupling. Future research should emphasize standardized datasets, uncertainty-aware fusion, sensor calibration, edge deployment, digital twins, and field validation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Abstract: Traditional airflow field measurement methods for cotton picker fans (e.g., Pitot tube method) can only obtain discrete point data and fail to collect full-flow field information; although Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation enables full-flow field analysis, it is restricted by high computational cost and long cycle, making real-time monitoring difficult. To address these issues, this study proposed a fast and accurate dynamic monitoring method for the airflow field at the outlet of cotton picker fans based on digital twin (DT) technology. Firstly, a high-fidelity CFD model of the centrifugal fan was established, and unsteady simulations were carried out across 1000-4000 r/min to obtain full-flow field data including velocity and pressure distributions. Secondly, four surrogate models— polynomial response surface (PRS), Radial Basis Function (RBF), Kriging (KRG) and support vector regression (SVR)—were compared to select the optimal one for fast airflow field prediction, and the fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering algorithm was introduced to screen representative core sampling nodes from the original dataset to reduce computational overhead. Thirdly, the optimized KRG model was encapsulated into a. NET standard class library by Matlab, and a windows forms (WinForm) human-machine interface (HMI) platform was developed via C# hybrid programming. Finally, a pneumatic conveying test bench was built, equipped with a PNP Hall effect sensor for rotational speed measurement, and combined with a planar guide rail system to collect high-precision wind speed data at key nodes, completing system performance verification. CFD simulation results showed that fan rotational speed correlated with the average wind speed in the central flow domain: the average wind speed increased approximately linearly at low rotational speeds, while growth slowed with nonlinear characteristics at high rotational speeds. With rising rotational speed, the wind speed difference at the outlet increased and inhomogeneity intensified, reaching 68.86% at 3 500 r/min. Among the four surrogate models, the KRG model performed best, with its root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) all lower than the others. Compared with uniform sampling, FCM clustering reduced training samples by 8.84%, improved response speed by 8.86% and decreased prediction error by 3.9353%. The monitoring system built with 821 clustered representative nodes had an average response time <1 s under all tested rotational speeds. Experimental verification indicated that the average prediction error between system output and measured values was within 9.26%, with the lowest error of 4.90% at 4 000 r/min. Dense grid tests at 3500 r/min showed that the relative error of most measurement points was still below 8% even near the volute tongue, where airflow separation and eddies frequently occurred. The proposed monitoring method effectively integrates CFD simulation, surrogate modeling and FCM clustering technology, enabling fast and accurate full-flow field monitoring of cotton picker fans. Its real-time response and prediction accuracy meet agricultural machinery operational requirements, providing technical support for monitoring and optimizing cotton picker pneumatic conveying systems, offering a transferable reference for airflow field monitoring of other agricultural equipment, and promoting digital twin technology in agricultural engineering. © 2026 Chinese Society of Agricultural Engineering. Title: One Health Cyber-Biotechnology for Nano-Plastic Intelligence Systems and Logic Integration: From Exposure to System-Level Interpretation
Source title: One Health Approaches to Nanoplastics Contamination: Biotechnological and AI Solutions
Affiliations: Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology Research Institute (GEBRI), City of Scientific Research and Technological Applications (SRTA-City), Alexandria, Egypt
Authors with affiliations: Reyed R.M., Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology Research Institute (GEBRI), City of Scientific Research and Technological Applications (SRTA-City), Alexandria, Egypt
Abstract: This chapter per the authors develops a One Health cyber-biotechnology framework for interpreting nanoplastic exposure as a multiscale environmentalsignaling system rather than an isolated contaminant phenomenon. It integrates digital nanoplastic science (DNPS), plasto-signaling interference (PSI), transductive signalload (TSL), Polybiome Interfacial Signaling Cascade (PISC), and systemic risk scoring (SRS) to structure exposure propagation, interface-level perturbation, and biological signaling disruption within a unified analytical architecture. Environmental matrices including water, soil, and air are conceptualized as dynamic signal-generating interfaces transmitting disturbances across interconnected ecological and physiological networks under uncertainty regimes. The chapter critiques conventional compartment-based risk assessment and advances multiomics integration, digital twin modeling, and cyber-biotechnological analytics for early-warning systems, exposure intelligence, and One Health–driven environmental decision support. Abstract: Accurate prediction of battery degradation, aging trajectories, and lifetime is critical for electrochemical energy storage systems, with direct implications for safety, reliability, and lifecycle cost. Although artificial intelligence (AI)–based approaches have shown strong short-term performance in state-of-health and remaining useful life estimation, many remain data-driven and show limited robustness under long-term cycling, operating-regime shifts, and extrapolation beyond training data. Physics-based degradation models provide mechanistic insight, but face challenges related to computational cost, parameter uncertainty, and scalability. This review positions physics-informed artificial intelligence (PIAI) as an integrative modeling paradigm that can improve data efficiency, physical consistency, uncertainty awareness, and decision reliability when appropriately constrained and validated. Unlike reviews that examine AI algorithms, degradation mechanisms, hybrid models, digital twins, or uncertainty-aware prognostics separately, this work provides a unified multiscale synthesis linking degradation physics, PIAI model construction, uncertainty quantification, structured validation, and BMS/digital-twin deployment. We examine how physical laws, degradation constraints, and uncertainty representations are embedded into learning architectures and analyze failure modes of black-box and poorly constrained hybrid models. The review proposes a five-layer framework for trustworthy battery lifetime prediction and identifies directions for physically credible, uncertainty-aware, and deployment-ready battery intelligence. © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: Partially automated truck fleets, consisting of both Automated Trucks (ATs) and Human-Driven Trucks (HDTs), are expected to be the operational norm in Automated Container Terminals (ACTs) for the foreseeable future. Right-of-Way (ROW) allocation has emerged as an effective approach for coordinating such heterogeneous fleets. However, existing ROW methods struggle to handle HDT-induced disruptions due to insufficient consideration of HDT behavioral uncertainties. To address this gap, this paper proposes a robust ROW allocation method tailored for mixed-traffic ACTs. The proposed method features: i) reduces conflicts involving uncertainties in turning intentions of HDTs; ii) addresses impedance caused by slow-moving HDTs; iii) achieves high computational efficiency while maintaining high solution quality. Methodologically, the proposed method is formulated as a three-stage stochastic optimization framework. First, an inference engine predicts the probabilities of HDT turning maneuvers. Second, a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is constructed to optimize passage timing, sequencing, and overtaking decisions across high-probability turning scenarios. To meet real-time computational demands, a customized Benders Branch-and-Cut (BB&C) algorithm is developed, enhanced with several acceleration strategies, including the generation of strong optimality cuts. Finally, a robustness criterion based on expected net benefit is employed to select the optimal allocation scheme under turning uncertainty. Simulation experiments based on a high-fidelity digital twin of a real-world terminal are conducted. Results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in conflict resolution, impedance mitigation, and terminal operational efficiency. Additionally, the operational feasibility domain regarding fleet size and HDT ratio is identified. Furthermore, the algorithm achieves millisecond-level computation times, confirming its feasibility for real-time deployment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Abstract: In this perspective, we present a concise, visionary abstract that highlights the challenge of ever-increasing complexity in future power grids and our proposed artificial intelligence for science (AI4S) framework. Next-generation grids, with high levels of renewables and distributed generation, create unprecedented uncertainty that strains traditional control and forecasting methods. Our AI4S framework integrates cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models (LLMs), physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), deep reinforcement learning (DRL), and autonomous multi-agent systems, within a domain-aware architecture that embeds grid physics, operational constraints, and human oversight into learning. By fusing data-driven models with power-system laws, AI4S yields trustworthy, explainable AI that enables fast, real-time decision making and richer situational awareness via digital twins and advanced forecasting. We distinguish which AI4S elements are already demonstrated versus conceptual, and we envision benefits like accelerated simulation, improved resilience, and greater operator trust. © 2026 THE AUTHORS. Abstract: Effective digital twin integration is increasingly critical for the optimal operation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as missions demand greater autonomy, endurance, and reliability. Traditional UAV battery health monitoring and control strategies rely primarily on onboard sensors, static voltage thresholds, conservative safety margins, and post-flight analysis. While these battery monitoring approaches provide baseline protection, they often result in overly conservative mission planning or reactive warnings that occur too late to prevent degradation or failure. Conventional monitoring methods frequently lack predictive capability, limiting their ability to provide actionable insight during dynamic flight conditions. To address these challenges, this work presents the development and ground-based validation of a propulsion subsystem digital twin integrated within the SWIFT-UAV (Scientific Workhorse for In-Flight Field Tests), a modular 3D printed UAV platform initially developed at the University of South Carolina. SWIFT-UAV’s open architecture, high payload capacity, and compatibility with advanced autonomy make it an ideal testbed for digital twin implementation. Rather than immediate in-flight deployment, the digital twin framework is evaluated using a propulsion iron-bird configuration that isolates the electrical power subsystem from aerodynamic and flight control uncertainties. Experimental measurements are compared against MATLAB/Simulink Simscape-based propulsion and battery models to assess predictive fidelity and identify discrepancies between modeled and observed behavior. Results demonstrate strong agreement between simulated and experimental data, supporting the feasibility of subsystem-level digital twin validation as a precursor to hardware-in-the-loop and eventual in-flight implementation. This work advances UAV energy management by transitioning from passive threshold-based monitoring toward predictive, model-informed battery endurance forecasting capable of supporting adaptive and energy-aware mission planning. © 2026, American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics Inc, AIAA. Abstract: Accurate prediction of emergency material demand after earthquakes is essential for effective disaster response following earthquakes is vital to disaster preparedness and relief activities; however, such forecasting can be difficult owing to lack of data, dynamic environment, and high uncertainties involved. Conventional models which depend on past experiences, along with static machine learning techniques, cannot adapt to changing situations and lack causal relationships. In this work, a new method called Causal Digital Twin-Driven Emergency Material Demand Prediction (CDT-EMDP) has been developed that incorporates causal reasoning, digital twin simulations, agent-based analysis, and Bayesian modeling to address the challenge. CDT-EMDP builds a causal graph showing the relationship between seismogenic intensity, damage, and human displacement. The simulation of a disaster scenario is conducted via digital twin, and the agent-based simulation predicts emergency material demands in an adaptive manner. Real-time feedback is used to refine predictions according to newly acquired data. The experiments conducted on the proposed method using simulated earthquake scenarios reveal that the model performs with an accuracy of 92.8%, outperforming traditional methods. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The fidelity of a digital twin is maintained by continuously updating the models embedded in its virtual entity with real-time sensor data. Conditional invertible neural networks (cINNs) offer a promising data-driven approach for likelihood-free model updating. However, they struggle to capture strong couplings among model parameters and often fail to effectively use suboptimal or limited sensor measurements. Additionally, epistemic uncertainty cannot be rigorously quantified in standard cINNs. To address these issues, an invertible attention-enhanced cINN (IA-cINN) is proposed. A novel invertible attention layer is integrated into the architecture. This layer explicitly models intrinsic correlations among model parameters and cross-dependencies between parameters and measurements through self- and cross-attention mechanisms while rigorously preserving invertibility. Monte Carlo dropout is incorporated into the IA-cINN to quantify epistemic uncertainty. The method was validated on two engineering cases. In a simulated case of a material handling device, three material parameters of structural components were updated using only strain and deformation measurements. In an experimental bearing case, contact stiffness, defect length, and radial clearance were updated using vibration features. In both cases, the IA-cINN outperformed the conventional cINN, as well as a Bayesian updating method based on Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. The IA-cINN achieved significantly higher updating accuracy, especially for parameters that exhibited complex coupling relationships with others. It produced more reliable uncertainty intervals in both cases, as indicated by lower interval scores. These intervals were shown to be sensitive to key sources of epistemic uncertainty, including data scarcity and insufficient model learning. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Abstract: Accurately estimating the cost of a construction project is crucially important to its ultimate success, and the integration of smart technologies such as Digital Twin (DT) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming the process by enabling real-time data and predictive insights. The adoption of these technologies, however, is being hindered by specific barriers that few studies have identified or modeled to determine their impact. This study addressed this gap by developing an ordinal logistic regression (OLR) model to predict the likelihood and degree of influence of DT-IoT system implementation challenges on construction estimating. The model used data derived from 135 responses from construction professionals in the United States to a survey that was designed to determine the impact on construction cost estimates of ten challenges that are incurred when implementing a DT-IoT system. The findings indicated that lack of cooperation, lack of team spirit, and inadequate communication are significant individual predictors of inaccurate and unreliable cost estimates. The most critical, however, was the combination of a lack of team spirit and insufficient funding, which was found to greatly undermine the reliability of cost estimation. Paradoxically, some factors such as the lack of a clear roadmap were positively associated with effective cost estimating, which may be because they lead to more cautious planning or increased monitoring that helps reduce uncertainty. The model provides a predictive tool that project managers and other industry professionals can use to refine their approaches to implementing a smart system that will improve the reliability and accuracy of their cost estimates. © ASCE.

Title: Closed-loop intelligent quality control for robotic welding: A survey on architecture, technologies, and system integration
Affiliations: School of Automation, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; School of Materials Science and Engineering, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China
Authors with affiliations: Qiu C., School of Automation, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; Zhou W., School of Automation, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; Yang L., School of Automation, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; Peng Y., School of Materials Science and Engineering, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; Wang K., School of Materials Science and Engineering, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China
Abstract: Weld quality formation involves strong multi-physics coupling under multiple sources of uncertainty. The conventional open-loop paradigm—pre-set parameters followed by post-weld inspection—therefore cannot deliver timely in-process intervention. Recent advances in multi-modal sensing, deep learning, advanced control, and digital twins have made closed-loop quality control technically feasible, yet integrating these isolated technologies into an end-to-end system remains a major challenge. Existing reviews predominantly address single functional layers and lack systematic analysis of cross-layer integration, engineering maturity, and fair evaluation protocols. We propose a unified analytical framework for robotic arc welding: a five-layer closed-loop architecture (Perception–Modeling–Decision–Execution–Assessment) coupled with three nested feedback loops (fast/medium/slow). We then review key technologies across all layers in a concept-centric manner: multi-modal sensing organized by physical observables and fusion hierarchy; physics-driven, data-driven, and hybrid modeling with trade-off analysis; hierarchical control from PID through MPC, ADRC, and reinforcement learning; and assessment covering inspection, diagnostics, and knowledge feedback. A Technology Readiness Level (TRL) assessment of over 40 technologies yields a maturity matrix with a pronounced “ends-high, middle-low” pattern. Inter-layer interface analysis exposes a critical asymmetry: the forward path from perception to execution is largely established, whereas the backward knowledge path from assessment to modeling/decision remains severely fragmented. Finally, we identify common pitfalls in method comparison and propose a two-tier comparison framework with a minimum reporting standard. We lay out a systematic roadmap for moving robotic welding from isolated single-layer demonstrations toward deployable and evolvable industrial closed-loop systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Quantification of Thermal and Water Leak Consequences in District Heating Systems Through Simulation: A Danish Case Study
Source title: IC3IT 2026 - Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Innovative and Intelligent Information Technologies
Affiliations: University of Southern Denmark, SDU Center for Energy Informatics, Odense, Denmark
Authors with affiliations: Sondergaard H.A.N., University of Southern Denmark, SDU Center for Energy Informatics, Odense, Denmark; Mortensen L.K., University of Southern Denmark, SDU Center for Energy Informatics, Odense, Denmark; Shaker H.R., University of Southern Denmark, SDU Center for Energy Informatics, Odense, Denmark
Abstract: Leakages in district heating pipes significantly impact system performance, leading to disruptions in heat supply to consumers and incurring continuous costs due to water loss. Unlike water distribution systems, DH leaks also result in heat losses, which require additional heat production and reduce operational efficiency. By quantifying the consequences, it becomes possible to evaluate whether they are relevant for risk assessment. Calculation of the risk of leakages can enable improved asset management by prioritizing pipes according to risk. To support this, this paper developed a digital twin of a district heating distribution system, simulating leakages using the orifice equation. From this, the water leakage rates and the extra production necessary to compensate for the water leakage could be determined, along with an estimation of the costs. Various experiments using a range of leakage characteristics were carried out to evaluate the costs. It was found that leakage characteristics drastically affect costs, but the costs are usually insignificant compared to excavation and repair. Furthermore, the calculated costs have high uncertainty, as there are many assumptions regarding the leakage characteristics. As a result, direct leakage costs are not appropriate for effective risk assessment. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Integrating kinetic ODEs in neural networks: A physics-informed hybrid approach to reactor modeling

Abstract: Mechanistic models of catalytic reactors are robust but often fail to generalize across feedstocks and operating conditions due to incomplete kinetic representations and parameter uncertainty, while purely data-driven models lack physical consistency and require large datasets that are costly to obtain in process engineering. To address these challenges, this work proposes a physics-informed hybrid framework that integrates a kinetic ordinary differential equation (ODE) into a neural network through automatic differentiation, differential residual loss minimization, and physical boundary constraints, taking both operating conditions and feedstock descriptors as inputs. The approach is applied to industrial hydrotreating (HDT), focusing on the prediction of nitrogen slip concentration in vacuum gas oil (VGO) hydrodenitrogenation (HDN). Two methodological developments are proposed: a Delaunay-triangulation-based strategy to select the input locations at which the physical residual and boundary terms are enforced during hybrid training, and a feedstock oriented evaluation across 30 randomized splits in which entire feedstocks are withheld from training to assess extrapolation. The hybrid model consistently outperforms both the mechanistic and purely data-driven baselines, achieving lower RMSE, MAE, and temperature deviations, while trend analyses confirm stronger preservation of the underlying physical dependencies, even under extrapolation to unseen feedstocks. A systematic comparison using a simplified kinetic formulation further shows that the hybrid architecture remains effective when constrained by incomplete mechanistic knowledge, outperforming data-driven models and approaching the accuracy of the complete kinetic expression. These results highlight the robustness, flexibility, and practical relevance of physics-informed hybrid modeling for reactor systems, offering a promising pathway toward reliable and quickly developed digital twins in catalytic process engineering. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Zhu T.; E W.
Title: From artificial intelligence for science to autonomous chemical innovation: closing the loop in energy and chemical engineering
Affiliations: School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, East China Normal University, 3663 North Zhongshan Road, Shanghai, 200062, China; AI for Science Institute, 150 Chengfu Road, Beijing, 100080, China
Authors with affiliations: Zhu T., School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, East China Normal University, 3663 North Zhongshan Road, Shanghai, 200062, China, AI for Science Institute, 150 Chengfu Road, Beijing, 100080, China; E W., AI for Science Institute, 150 Chengfu Road, Beijing, 100080, China
Abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly capable of predicting chemical properties, generating candidate structures, and assisting experimental planning. Yet the rate-limiting step in energy and chemical innovation is no longer prediction alone: it is the conversion of computational proposals into reproducible experiments and deployable process decisions. In this Perspective, we argue that Artificial Intelligence for Science in chemistry is undergoing a decisive transition from model-centric performance improvement to executable, closed-loop research infrastructure. This transition involves three coupled layers. First, physically grounded models must connect molecular and materials structures with energetics, kinetics, experimental observations, and uncertainty. Second, design algorithms must operate in validation-aware workflows that link inverse design, mechanistic computation, experimentation, and process constraints. Third, autonomous laboratories require reusable agent infrastructure that integrates scientific software, instruments, analytical feedback, safety control, and human accountability. We discuss developments in molecular and catalyst design, reaction optimization, digital twins, and self-driving laboratories, and identify data provenance, physical execution, reliability benchmarking, and safety governance as central translational challenges. For energy and chemical engineering, the value of artificial intelligence will ultimately be determined not by the number of candidates it proposes, but by its ability to close the loop from hypothesis to validated technology. © The Author(s) 2026. Title: Subgroup division-based cooperative consensus control for mixed vehicle groups with heterogeneous spacing policy and delay compensation under digital twin network

Authors with affiliations: Huang S., College of Artificial Intelligence, Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Chongqing, 400065, China, Institute of Industrial Internet, Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Chongqing, 401120, China, Key Laboratory of Big Data Intelligent Computing, Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Chongqing, 400065, China; Li Y., College of Automation, Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Chongqing, 400065, China; Feng Y., College of Integrated Circuits, Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Chongqing, 400065, China
Abstract: To ensure the stability of three types of heterogeneous vehicles with different information acquisition capabilities, control mechanisms, and delay effects, this paper proposes a mixed vehicle group cooperative consensus control strategy based on subgroup division rules by employing digital twin technology. Firstly, the mixed vehicle group consisting of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs), autonomous vehicles (AVs), and traditional human-driven vehicles (HVs) is taken as the research object; it is divided into multiple logical subgroups to facilitate analyzing the cooperative driving relationship among heterogeneous vehicles within each subgroup and between subgroups. Thereafter, to guarantee that heterogeneous vehicles can quickly track different desired inter-vehicle distances, a heterogeneous spacing strategy is designed. Meanwhile, the improved HV, CAV, and AV models are established by considering the randomness and uncertainty of human drivers, as well as the impact of heterogeneous delays. Subsequently, to mitigate the impact of heterogeneous delays on the stability of mixed vehicle groups, a cooperative consensus control strategy is developed based on the delay compensation mechanism under a digital twin network. Lastly, the conditions of string stability among heterogeneous vehicles within subgroups and between subgroups are derived to ensure the stability of cooperative driving of the mixed vehicle group composed of CAVs, AVs and HVs. The simulation results show that the proposed method can ensure collision-free tracking of heterogeneous desired intervehicle distances of 13 m, 14 m, and 16 m for CAVs, AVs, and HVs within approximately 24 s, 17 s, and 28 s within the mixed vehicle group consisting of 13 heterogeneous vehicles. This result further verifies the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Abstract: The deep integration of high-resolution Earth observation, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things is propelling remote sensing geological exploration from traditional single-satellite data interpretation towards a new paradigm of space-air-ground collaborative observation and intelligent multi-source data analysis. This paper systematically reviews the key progress of the integrated "space-based (satellites), air-based (aviation/ UAVs), and ground-based (surface sensing)" remote sensing technology system in the field of mineral exploration. The discussion focuses on three primary aspects: (1) Breakthroughs in platform and sensor technologies, particularly the advancements in hyperspectral, LiDAR, and synthetic aperture radar, along with their collaborative observation mechanisms and current applications; (2) Innovations in intelligent data processing methods, encompassing fusion techniques for multi-source heterogeneous data, as well as AI-driven extraction of mineral information and metallogenic prediction models; (3) Establishment and practice of application paradigms, summarizing successful case studies of this technology in complex scenarios such as covered areas, deep-seated zones, and special landscape regions. This has led to the development of a standardized technical workflow: "satellite-based wide-area screening→UAV-based detailed survey→ground-based target validation." Building on this systematic review, the paper further analyzes the core technological bottlenecks currently hindering development. These primarily include the lack of standardization in multi-source data fusion, difficulties in quantifying prediction uncertainty, and the weak interpretability of intelligent geological models (the "black box" problem). Looking forward, the paper discusses future development trends, highlighting that real-time, intelligent, and digital-twin-enabled smart exploration, along with the construction of satellite constellation-coordinated intelligent observation networks, will become important drivers of innovation in remote sensing technology for mineral exploration. In conclusion, this intelligent space-air-ground integrated remote sensing technology system is fundamentally transforming traditional exploration paradigms, providing critical scientific and technological support for solving exploration challenges in complex geological settings and ensuring national mineral resource security. © (2026), (Editorial Board of Geology and Exploration). Title: The Impact and Integration of AI: From Research to Realization in Clinical Trials
Source title: The Impact and Integration of AI: From Research to Realization
Affiliations: Golden Gate University, India
Authors with affiliations: Bidarkund N., Golden Gate University, India; Das D., Golden Gate University, India; Khanna S., Golden Gate University, India
Abstract: This article provides a comprehensive overview of AI’s evolving role in clinical trials. will trace the evolution of AI technologies relevant to clinical research, from the rise of deep neural networks to the emergence of digital twins and generative AI. We then delve into practical applications across the clinical trial continuum – including real-world case studies of AI-driven trial innovations – and examine how leading organizations are leveraging AI today. Alongside the opportunities, we address the challenges and ethical considerations (such as data privacy, bias, and regulatory uncertainty) that must be managed for AI to truly transform clinical development. Finally, we offer a forward-looking perspective on the future of AI in clinical trials, outlining how upcoming advances and collaborative efforts can further integrate AI into clinical research in a safe, effective, and ethical manner. Abstract: Nanofluids are innovative materials consisting of a suspension of nanoparticles in a fluid, such as water or oil. They are commonly used in engineering and medicine because of their thermal conductivity, which makes them particularly efficient for cooling, heat transport, and tumor treatment. In recent times, the unique properties of nanofluids have led to their use for environmental application. This includes oil extraction processes, the treatment of contaminated water and soil, and the improvement of the seismic response of the soil during strong seismic events. Although these applications are very different from each other, it is necessary in all cases to inject the nanoparticles into the soil. However, predicting the distribution of particles a priori, considering the injection parameters, is very difficult due to the intrinsic complexity of the subsoil and uncertainty regarding parameters such as porosity and elastic properties. One possible solution is to use numerical simulations on digital twins of the area of interest. These simulations are computationally expensive, and are affected, in the specific case, by a high level of uncertainty, due to the lack of specific information on soil stratigraphy. In this paper, we present and discuss a mathematical model that describes the injection of nanofluid into the soil, taking into account its natural poroelasticity, which is often neglected. The subsequent drift and diffusion of the particles, as well as their interaction with the surrounding medium through absorption and desorption processes, can be described using the same model, but with different boundary and initial conditions. After introducing the model, we discuss in detail the effects of poroelasticity and the role of injection parameters on particle distribution. We also present some (semi−)analytical representations of the model that could be useful for the preliminar calibration of the numerical simulations and, potentially, of the injection process. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Title: Design of an Integrated Model for Validation Driven Control and Certification of Hybrid AC-DC Microgrids

Affiliations: Prmceam Badnera-Amravati, Department of Electrical Engineering, Maharashtra, India; Government College of Engineering Amravati, Department of Electrical Engineering, Maharashtra, India
Authors with affiliations: Dahane A.S., Prmceam Badnera-Amravati, Department of Electrical Engineering, Maharashtra, India; Sharma R.B., Government College of Engineering Amravati, Department of Electrical Engineering, Maharashtra, India
Abstract: In fast converter switching, volatile renewable injections, frequent mode changes, and partial observability, hybrid AC-DC microgrids must behave like a power systems. This tension requires validation frameworks beyond nominal models and idealized control assumptions. Most research used fixedparameter simulations, poorly coupled digital twins, or controller tuning evaluated under limited disturbance sets, which seems to leave a gap between stated performance and field behavior, especially at AC-DC interfaces. A, chained validation and control treats model mismatch, uncertainty and explainability as a key signals, but not subsidiary issues. In this paper a five-step analytical procedure is established. Here, hybrid Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) Twin-Fidelity Calibrator calibrates parameters and structures residual fingerprints by aligning averaged and electromagnetic transient models. This residual goes directly into a Residual-Aware Distributionally Constrained Hybrid MPC (Model Predictive Control), where Wasserstein ambiguity impacts control decisions under observed deviations rather than presumed noise. Causal Graph Neural State and Fault Trajectories and constraint-activity traces are processed by the attribution layer to isolate strong instability drivers while maintaining physical directionality across AC and DC subsystems. Based on this belief state, a Barrier-Certified Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning coordinator adjusts converter operations during fast transients while respecting safety invariants in the process. To generate safety margins instead of qualitative statements, a Hybrid Contract Verification and Counterfactual Stress Prover evaluates learned rules against targeted adversarial scenarios. Experimental validation on representative hybrid microgrid shows lower voltage and frequency excursions, faster post islanding recovery, and quantified safe operating envelope extensions. Evidence-driven, falsification-aware microgrid control designs may replace performance-centric validation. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: A digital-twin framework for efficient prediction of field-level quantities in pump-turbine systems using a reduced-order modeling (ROM) approach is presented in this paper. The framework couples a steady parametric proper-orthogonal-decomposition reduced-order model (POD-ROM) with a phase-locked Fourier representation of transient blade loading, enabling fast reconstruction of blade-surface pressure and velocity distributions across operating conditions. Pressure and velocity are used only as representative demonstration variables; the same workflow applies to other monitored scalar or vector quantities, provided the field of interest admits an accurate low-rank (linear) approximation. Under leave-one-out validation at the design condition, the steady POD-ROM reproduces the CFD reference with a global relative (Formula presented) error of 0.55% for pressure and 3.0% for velocity, with coefficients of determination R2of 0.997 and 0.991, respectively; the larger pointwise velocity percentiles are confined to low-momentum regions and do not affect the global or mechanical-integrity-relevant fidelity. The model extrapolates accurately for small excursions beyond the sampled range, is well-conditioned against input-parameter uncertainty (normalised sensitivity below unity), and inherits an intrinsic denoising capability from POD truncation. For transient loading, the phase-locked Fourier "twin state" compresses rotor-synchronous pulsations—at the design and two off-design conditions—into a compact, physically interpretable coefficient set, reconstructing the phase-resolved loading with sub-percent error while retaining cycle-to-cycle variability. Once the offline stage is complete, online inference reduces a full CFD evaluation from hours to seconds or less, making the framework well suited to real-time digital-twin deployment for predictive maintenance and operational optimization. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: A digital twin-based comparative reinforcement learning framework for personalized behavioral recommendation
Affiliations: Department of Digital Technology, Norwegian Institute for Air Research, Kjeller, Norway; Inland School of Business and Social Sciences, University of Inland Norway, Lillehammer, Norway
Authors with affiliations: Chatterjee A., Department of Digital Technology, Norwegian Institute for Air Research, Kjeller, Norway; Avazov N., Inland School of Business and Social Sciences, University of Inland Norway, Lillehammer, Norway
Abstract: Promoting healthy lifestyle behaviors such as physical activity, sleep, diet quality, stress management, hydration, and healthy habits requires adaptive systems capable of responding dynamically to changing behavioral and environmental conditions. However, the development and evaluation of personalized recommendation systems are challenged by fragmented observational data, privacy constraints, delayed feedback, and ethical limitations associated with long-term human experimentation. To address these challenges, this study proposes a digital twin-driven reinforcement learning framework for generating personalized behavioral recommendations in a fully simulated and statistically validated environment. The proposed framework formulates personalized behavioral recommendation as a stochastic Markov Decision Process (MDP) incorporating adherence uncertainty, behavioral drift, environmental modulation, and engagement dynamics. Synthetic longitudinal behavioral trajectories are generated through a digital twin simulator that models demographic heterogeneity, lifestyle behaviors, contextual variables, and variability in policy adherence over time. The optimization objective is defined through an effective reward formulation that balances behavioral compliance gains against penalties associated with health and environmental constraint violations. This study implements several reinforcement learning (RL) paradigms under simulated conditions, such as multi-armed bandits, table-based Q-learning, State-Action-Reward-State-Action (SARSA), function approximation-based temporal difference (TD) learning, and deep Q-learning network (DQN). The results demonstrate that richer state representations and context-dependent action dynamics are necessary for higher-capacity reinforcement learning models to consistently outperform simpler baselines. Furthermore, this study provides a reproducible method for comparing learning dynamics, performance, and computational cost in digital twin-based recommender systems. The framework additionally supports privacy-preserving experimentation through the exclusive use of synthetic behavioral data and locally controlled simulation environments. Title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Digital Twins Engineering: Workflow Patterns, Gaps, and Research Opportunities

Affiliations: Institute of Information Technology, Riga Technical University, Riga, Latvia
Authors with affiliations: Korcevskis M., Institute of Information Technology, Riga Technical University, Riga, Latvia; Pecerska J., Institute of Information Technology, Riga Technical University, Riga, Latvia
Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into Digital Twin systems to enhance monitoring, prediction, optimization, and decision-making across industrial and infrastructure domains. However, existing research often reports AI-enabled Digital Twins within isolated application contexts, resulting in limited conceptual clarity regarding how AI methods align with the overall Digital Twin engineering workflow. This paper provides a focused conceptual synthesis of recent representative publications and organizes AI integration using a workflow-oriented analytical lens. Four dominant integration patterns are identified: AI-enhanced state estimation, hybrid data-driven modelling, reinforcement learning-based optimization, and AI-supported decision orchestration. Across domains, recurring challenges include workflow fragmentation, validation of embedded AI components, uncertainty management, interoperability, economic justification, and cybersecurity concerns. The findings highlight the need for architecture-level integration, standardized validation approaches, and governance-Aware design principles to support robust and scalable AI-enabled Digital Twins.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Mathematical Optimisation Framework for Energy Consumption Prediction in Smart Sustainable Systems

Abstract: Operational decarbonisation in smart sustainable systems depends on reliable short-horizon decisions under uncertainty. Such decisions remain high-leverage for buildings because of their large share of global energy use and emissions [3], [4]. The paper presents a hybrid framework combining day-ahead consumption prediction with a peak-aware mathematical scheduling layer. This predictor applies gradient-boosted regression to capture the nonlinear interactions of temporal structure, exogenous drivers, and lagged consumption. Adaptive residual quantiles on a rolling window measure uncertainty and form lower and upper envelopes that are responsive to drift in behaviour and regime. The optimization layer developed for PV-battery dispatch is linear program which minimizes energy cost penalizes peak grid import subject to battery dynamics power limits and state-of-charge limits. A strong variant is scheduled against the upper envelope in order to reduce peak violations in the event of forecast error. The suggested predictor makes a 4.06 kW RMSE persistence; 8.72 kW; ridge; 5.96 on a 15-minute digital-twin dataset. The mean cost is reduced by 2.64 % and peak import reduced by 11.13 % over the period of 14 days when the solution is coupled optimised, while robust planning reduces the peak-limit exceedance by half. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: With the promotion of decarbonization initiatives, many ports are building green shipping corridors (GSCs), which involve the adoption of clean energy and the development of supporting infrastructure between ports. However, uncertainties in clean energy supply costs pose challenges for strategic decision-making. In response, digital twin (DT) technologies, increasingly emphasized in port planning and management, help address these uncertainties by enhancing the availability and quality of information for decision-making. This study considers the information value of DT in GSCs construction, and uses game theory to analyze the strategy selection of two competitive ports in construction of GSCs. We find, first, when the traditional energy adoption ratio is small and in a certain interval, the port with GSCs obtains benefits and gives its opponent without GSCs an interesting free-rider effect thus forming a win–win outcome. Therefore, the practices that both ports conduct GSCs and only one port conducts GSCs can form two interesting win–win outcomes. Besides, when the traditional energy adoption is very small, i.e., below a certain threshold, the port with GSCs has huge competition advantages, thus only one port conducting GSCs will yield a win-lose outcome. Second, under perfect information with DT, many of the win–win outcomes observed under imperfect information are replaced by win-lose results. This suggests that access to accurate clean energy cost information diminishes the free-rider effect of the opponent without GSCs. Third, counter-intuitively, when the market size is large, DT may be over-invested if both two ports adopt DT, and information asymmetry may be better. These findings offer practical implications for port managers considering GSCs construction strategies under conditions of competition and information asymmetry. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Multi-scale sequential Bayesian method for parameter calibration; [基于多尺度序贯贝叶斯的数字孪生模型参数校正方法]

Abstract: Digital twin technology has been widely applied to the operational optimization of industrial processes, especially in process monitoring, performance prediction and fault tracing, where model accuracy directly affects application performance. However, industrial process models established from physicochemical mechanisms usually involve idealized assumptions and contain many undetermined parameters that must be calibrated using field measurements. To address the high computational cost of traditional Bayesian calibration in high-dimensional parameter spaces and its limited suitability for online rolling updates, a multiscale sequential Bayesian model parameter calibration method based on Gaussian process convolution was proposed. Within a Bayesian framework, the proposed method jointly characterized parameter uncertainty, model structural discrepancy and observation error, and the rolling correction was performed according to the deviation between model outputs and process observations. By introducing a multiscale model representation, the method enabled a flexible trade-off between calibration accuracy and computational efficiency under limited computational resources. Numerical simulation and an alumina evaporation process case study showed that the proposed method could separately represent the model output term and the systematic discrepancy term, while achieving efficient calibration with high prediction accuracy. Compared with the standard KOH method, the proposed method improved calibration efficiency by about 165, providing effective support for the high-fidelity operation of complex industrial digital twins. © 2025, CIMS. Abstract: Reliable real-time analysis of sensor data is essential for structural health monitoring (SHM) of high-value assets, where accurate prediction of the target field and uncertainty quantification are required for trustworthy decision-making. Such capabilities can help prevent structural fracture while reducing unnecessary maintenance and resource consumption. To reconstruct the target full-field from sparse sensor measurements, the high-dimensional full-field response is compressed into leading modes using principal component analysis (PCA). A Bayesian neural network (BNN) is then employed to predict these leading PCA modes from the sensor data. The parameters of the BNN are learned through pre-training followed by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling, allowing reconstruction of the target full-field with uncertainty quantification. Data-inherent aleatoric uncertainty is quantified through mode-wise variances during the pre-training stage, while epistemic uncertainty is quantified during HMC sampling. The framework was validated through cyclic four-point bending tests on carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) specimens with varying crack lengths. The experimental data comprised sparse strain gauge measurements and high-dimensional strain fields. Based on these data, the framework achieved accurate strain field reconstruction (R² > 0.9) while simultaneously producing real-time uncertainty fields, remaining robust under sparse and noisy measurements. In addition, the full-field aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty estimates enable local diagnosis of whether low-confidence regions are driven by data-inherent noise or model-related limitations. Collectively, the results demonstrate that the proposed framework advances SHM toward trustworthy digital twin deployment and risk-aware structural diagnostics. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Korean Society for Precision Engineering 2026.

Title: Autonomous Multi-Agent Coordination for Dynamic Construction Project Scheduling Under Resource Constraints and Environmental Uncertainties
Affiliations: Construction Project Management, University of Portsmouth, London, United Kingdom
Authors with affiliations: Sepehri M., Construction Project Management, University of Portsmouth, London, United Kingdom
Abstract: The research proposes a new autonomous multi-agent framework that combines distributed AI algorithms and real-time construction project data to support scheduling decisions in a complex constraint environment. The framework employs a blockchain-based coordination protocol that enables reinforcement learning agents to adapt schedules and allocate resources dynamically, requiring only supervisory human oversight for exception handling. The framework was validated in a digital twin simulation environment parameterized from 47 completed construction projects using historical project data, supplemented by a prospective six-project pilot deployment to assess real-world feasibility. From the implementation, project delays have reduced by 34% and resource utilization efficiency improved by 28%. The methodology integrates stochastic modeling of weather, the supply chain, and labor into the decision-making process. Each agent specializes in domains such as materials procurement, equipment scheduling, and quality control. The architecture makes use of federated learning principles that help maintain data privacy and allow collective intelligence across project sites. The results of validation indicate major improvements in cost-performance indices and schedule variance. The framework provides real-time adaptive scheduling solutions to unexpected site challenges, addressing a critical gap in current construction management practice. Copyright © 2026 Mehran Sepehri. Abstract: Lifecycle performance of ceramic matrix composites (CMCs) in extreme environments is dictated by coupled thermo-mechanical, chemical, and environmental degradation mechanisms, which cannot be accurately predicted by single-physics models. In this review, recent advances in multiphysics phase-field (PF) modeling of CMCs are evaluated, emphasizing thermo-mechanical fracture, oxidation-assisted degradation, chemo-mechanical coupling, electro-chemo-mechanical interactions, interfacial damage, and microstructural evolution. Fundamental PF theories, including variational, interface-aware PF-CZM, and thermodynamically-consistent coupled models, are presented alongside advancements in adaptive simulations, multi-scale modeling, machine-learning acceleration, uncertainty quantification, and digital twins. It is demonstrated that multiphysics PF models effectively predict crack evolution, chemical degradation, interface debonding, oxide formation, and environmental stiffness changes in complex CMC architectures. Furthermore, 3D microstructure-resolved modeling capabilities have been enhanced by adaptive discretization, high-performance computing, and surrogate learning. However, substantial challenges remain, including oversimplified multi-species chemistry, high computational costs of fully coupled 3D simulations, parameter non-uniqueness, and inadequate experimental validation under service conditions. Moving forward, further development would require the use of scalable Multiphysics PF modeling frameworks combined with physics-informed machine learning, uncertainty-aware calibration, adaptive data assimilation, and digital twin approaches, supporting the intelligent design of resilient infrastructures operating under extreme thermo-chemo-mechanical conditions. © 2026 The Author(s)

Abstract: Recent progresses in applying artificial intelligence (AI) to meteorological monitoring, forecasting, post-processing, and environmental services at Chinese Academy of Meteorological Sciences are reviewed. In data sensing and preprocessing, AI techniques are employed to learn radar and satellite features to improve sea-clutter identification, spatiotemporally consistent reconstruction of missing observations, and intelligent retrieval of key variables such as negative oxygen ions and land-surface temperature, improving the quality, continuity, and operational usability of datasets. For nowcasting/short-term forecasting, extrapolation integrating generative adversarial networks and physical constraints, and deep learning-numerical weather prediction coupled frameworks are being explored. For post-processing, Dice loss and multimodel ensemble correction are used to alleviate extreme-precipitation class imbalance and dust-forecast uncertainty, while deep error correction also improves El Niño-Southern Oscillation and regional precipitation forecasts. For end-to-end global AI forecasting, a modular assimilation-forecast cycle model (Fengyuan) has been developed to build an observation-to-forecast pipeline, thereby reducing dependence on numerical analysis fields. Cross-disciplinary progress is also highlighted, including long-term terrestrial water storage reconstruction, atmospheric pollution attribution, and first machine-learning-driven global aerosol-meteorology model, which together support water-resource and environmental management. Building on this progress, AI application to meteorology is moving from a post-processing aid to a driver of operational transformation, yet significant bottlenecks persist. Future progress should advance along 4 strategic directions. First, physical constraints must be more deeply embedded to improve interpretability and physical credibility alongside predictive accuracy, including tighter coupling of differentiable physical processes, conservation constraints, and deep neural networks. Second, the assimilation-forecast chain should move toward fuller observation-driven end-to-end framework, with expanded direct use of heterogeneous observations, flow-dependent error modeling, and reduced reliance on reanalysis fields. Third, deterministic mean prediction should be supplemented by probabilistic generative forecasting, integrating diffusion models, adversarial learning, and imbalance-aware strategies to better capture lowprobability, high-impact extremes and improve the reliability of early warnings. Fourth, AI meteorology should expand toward coupled multi-sphere applications, integrating atmosphere, land, hydrology, chemistry, ocean, cryosphere, and human-activity drivers to support digital-twin-enabled earth-system services. Next-stage development should be anchored in high-quality observations, physics-aware intelligent modeling, and rigorous validation across multiple scenarios. Improving Fengyuan in terms of resolution, lead time, stability and interpretability can more effectively support disaster risk reduction, carbon-neutral transition planning, energy scheduling, ecological governance, and high-quality development of weather services. Meanwhile, open benchmarking protocols, reproducible workflows, and cross-regional transfer evaluation frameworks are essential to ensure that Fengyuan delivers more robust and reliable performance under diverse climatic and operational scenarios. © 2026 Editorial Office of Journal of Applied Meteorological Science. Title: Prediction of cooking-induced food transformations: A survey and outlook towards machine learning
Affiliations: Multitel Research & Innovation Center, Artificial Intelligence Department, Belgium; Université Libre de Bruxelles (ULB), Transfers, Interfaces and Processes (TIPs), Belgium; Wallonia Institute of Food Science and Technology (WIFST), Belgium

Abstract: Cooking induces coupled physical, chemical, and biological transformations that jointly determine food safety, nutritional value, and sensory quality. Predicting cooking-induced food transformations is therefore a central challenge, receiving growing attention across applications including process optimisation in the food industry, product design, quality control, personalised cooking, and the development of smart appliances and digital twins. Despite extensive progress in food process engineering, robust prediction across foods, geometries, and operating conditions remains difficult due to the multiscale heterogeneity of food matrices, substantial process variability, and experimental data that are often sparse, noisy, or destructive to acquire. To stimulate future research, this survey provides a comprehensive review of modelling approaches for cooking-induced transformations and articulates a structured outlook towards machine learning (ML). We first consolidate the scientific background on food cooking processes. We then introduce a principled taxonomy of conventional models and analyse how their encoded structure can act as inductive bias for data-driven learning. Building on this foundation, we formalise cooking prediction as learning mappings from initial product state and process descriptors to time-resolved or endpoint outcomes, and synthesise data modalities and evaluation protocols required for trustworthy generalisation under distribution shift. Finally, we systematically map existing ML-based predictors, review hybrid and physics-informed integration strategies, and propose a research roadmap towards data-efficient, physically consistent, and uncertainty-aware models that enable robust decision-making and scalable digital twins for cooking processes. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Physics-Informed Bayesian Markov random field approach for road flooding inference from sparse post-disaster observations

Abstract: Extreme weather events increasingly threaten critical infrastructure, necessitating rapid and accurate assessment of transportation network damage for effective emergency response. However, such assessments are challenged by sparse and unevenly distributed post-disaster observation data. While data-driven and physics-based approaches offer possible solutions, they often face difficulties in integrating diverse domain knowledge and generalizing effectively under data-scarce conditions. This study proposes a Markov Random Field (MRF) framework to infer probabilistic flood inundation states from sparse observations. The model integrates geospatial information on elevation, physical principles governing hydrological flows, and topological characteristics of intersection vulnerability within a unified energy-based framework. Evaluation on Hurricane Harvey’s impact to Houston’s highway system indicates that the MRF model achieves consistently high predictive performance across varying levels of data sparsity. Specifically, with 40% observational data, the integration of hydrological and topological priors yielded an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.747, significantly surpassing the baseline elevation-only model (IoU = 0.517). The model also supports sequential updating of state estimates and parameters via Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling, allowing continuous refinement of inference results as new observational data becomes available. Furthermore, the probabilistic outputs support flexible, threshold-based risk classification, enabling adaptive decision-making for emergency resource allocation and laying the groundwork for digital twin applications. This work offers a transferable, knowledge-aware methodology for infrastructure resilience assessment under uncertainty. © 2026 The Author(s).

Title: A regime-aware digital twin for uncertainty-calibrated prediction and replay-based virtual commissioning of variable-capacity vapour-compression systems

Abstract: Variable-capacity vapour-compression systems expose strong dynamic coupling among compressor speed, valve opening, pressures, heat-transfer boundaries and safety variables. For control use, a one-step fit is not enough. The predictor also needs to track regimes, quantify uncertainty, adapt to drift and screen candidate actions. A regime-aware dynamic twin (RADT) pipeline is developed here from campaign-scale experiments on a variable-capacity vapour-compression rig. Physics-weighted K-means separates the operating regimes, and the 11-output RADT is trained with grouped state variables, pressure-derived features, a condenser-informed feature, ensemble aggregation and physics-corrected fine-tuning. Ensemble intervals are then calibrated by regime, a lightweight residual layer updates key outputs online, and the RADT is embedded in RADT-based real-time iteration sequential quadratic programming (RTI-SQP) for virtual commissioning. The chronological test set contains 1864 transitions from eight campaign blocks. One-step coefficient of determination (R2) reached 0.9855 for compressor power and 0.9125 for evaporator cooling capacity. For suction superheat and discharge temperature, R2 reached 0.9879 and 0.9764. Regime-conditioned conformal calibration increased mean 90% coverage from 83.6% to 96.4%, including a rise from 36.5% to 98.0% for condensing saturation temperature. On a 482-transition late-period shift subset, online correction reduced the mean root mean squared error (RMSE) of the four corrected outputs by 46.5%. In eight-block replay, predicted energy use fell by 3.8%, from 4768.2 to 4587.0 kW-steps. Mean coefficient of performance (COP) rose from 3.318 to 3.455, and superheat violations dropped from 297 to 78. RADT can be used to screen candidate control actions on historical campaign data before plant testing. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Digital twin stackelberg bayesian coordination of mobile storage for uncertainty-resilient renewable integration in offshore and coastal green hydrogen energy hubs
Affiliations: Energy Management Research Center, University of Mohaghegh Ardabili, Ardabil, Iran
Authors with affiliations: Shayeghi H., Energy Management Research Center, University of Mohaghegh Ardabili, Ardabil, Iran; Mohamadi B., Energy Management Research Center, University of Mohaghegh Ardabili, Ardabil, Iran; Zare P., Energy Management Research Center, University of Mohaghegh Ardabili, Ardabil, Iran
Abstract: The rapid deployment of renewable energy in offshore and coastal regions increases the need for storage systems that can manage intermittency, spatial mismatch, and grid integration constraints. Coordinated operation across offshore, coastal, and land-based energy hubs remains insufficiently developed when mobile storage logistics, green hydrogen pathways, multi-carrier coupling, and market mechanisms are considered together. This study proposes a digital twin-enabled optimization framework for mobile and hybrid storage management in offshore and coastal multi-energy communities. The architecture integrates electrical, thermal, cooling, hydrogen, and water subsystems, while offshore energy transport vessels relocate mobile storage units and support dynamic energy exchange among distributed hubs. A mixed-integer optimization model determines storage scheduling, inter-hub exchange, desalination operation, grid interaction, and market participation. A Stackelberg-Bayesian structure captures hierarchical interactions and information asymmetry among hubs, while a Wasserstein distance-based robust optimization framework handles uncertainty in renewable generation, demand, and market prices. Carbon emission trading and green certificate trading are embedded as market-based decarbonization incentives. Numerical results show that coordinated mobile storage operation improves renewable utilization and flexibility, eliminates curtailed electrical loads, and reduces operating costs by up to 21% compared with non-coordinated operation. Under environmental constraints, groundwater extraction is fully eliminated, with the cost increase partly offset by carbon and green certificate revenues. Coordinated operation increases carbon trading revenues by approximately 27% and green certificate revenues by up to 54%. These findings show that digital twin Stackelberg-Bayesian coordination of mobile storage can strengthen uncertainty-resilient renewable integration in offshore and coastal green hydrogen energy hubs. © 2026

Abstract: State-of-the-art schemes for the performance analysis and optimization of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications generally suffer from degradation or even become ineffective in highly dynamic and complex environments with unknown interference and uncertain channel state information (CSI). To address these challenges and enhance network self-optimization, we propose a learnable model-driven regularized zero-forcing precoding scheme, and design a light-weight neural network for refined prediction of sum rate and detection error, by leveraging coarse model-driven approximations. Then, we estimate the CSI uncertainty based on the learned predictor in an iterative manner and, in turn, optimize both the transmit regularization term and subsequent receive power scaling factors. To achieve a favorable trade-off between convergence speed and robustness, we further propose a deep-unfolded projected gradient descent algorithm for power scaling. © 2015 Chinese Institute of Electronics.

Abstract: Fatigue failures in resistance spot welds represent a critical challenge in automotive design, yet current evaluation methods typically consider only nominal geometries and neglect manufacturing-induced variability. This study investigates the influence of geometric variations on fatigue-life prediction by combining linear-elastic notch stress analysis using a simplified notch and regression-based surrogate modeling. The approach targets high-cycle fatigue dominated by elastic stress concentrations requiring precise simulated peak stress evaluation. A D-optimal design of experiments was conducted with seven geometric design variables, including sheet thickness, notch radius, electrode indentation, nugget diameter, electrode diameter, and the inner and outer gaps. In total, 80 simulations were performed to assess notch stress and electrode indentation stress as response variables. Quadratic regression models achieved coefficients of determination R 2 > 0.99 for both responses. The models reveal that parameter significance changes with boundary conditions, such as constant force or stress, that affect the critical area. The 95 % confidence band for notch stress widens from about 3 % in the central design space to approximately 6 % for thinner sheets and increased electrode indentation. Incorporating realistic parameter deviations substantially improves fatigue-life prediction reliability and enables quantitative assessment of uncertainty. The proposed framework establishes a variability-aware methodology that integrates simulation and regression analysis into spot weld design, advancing beyond current nominal-value-based practices. While the present work focuses on stress prediction and variability, the simulated notch stresses can subsequently be combined with experimental S-N data by reproducing the test geometry and loading in the simulation, thereby enabling direct fatigue-life assessment within the same conceptual framework. © 2026 The Authors.
