Abstract: Real-time prediction of full-field stress and strain responses is essential for digital twin applications in metro bogie structures. However, existing data-driven approaches face two key challenges: handling extremely high-dimensional finite element outputs with strong spatial correlations, and achieving reliable real-time inference while preserving physical interpretability and uncertainty awareness. To address these challenges, this study proposes a physics-informed deep learning framework for fast and reliable full-field stress/strain prediction under operational conditions. The framework integrates a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a finite element–based graph neural network (FEMGNN). The CNN extracts compact latent features from multi-channel vibration signals, while the FEMGNN represents finite element nodes as graph vertices and incorporates element stiffness into edge weights to capture structural topology and physical coupling. By embedding physical and topological information into the learning process, the proposed model enables end-to-end mapping from vibration measurements to node-level stress/strain fields, eliminating the need for independent node-wise modeling and improving both accuracy and computational efficiency. The method can predict full-field responses at more than 18,000 nodes in a single forward pass, with an average inference time of approximately 2.38 ms on a workstation GPU, demonstrating real-time inference potential for digital-twin-based structural monitoring. Furthermore, Monte Carlo Dropout is employed to estimate both predictive means and associated uncertainties, enabling spatial uncertainty visualization and confidence interval analysis. Numerical results under normal operating conditions and multiple crack scenarios demonstrate that the proposed CNN–FEMGNN achieves overall competitive and stable full-field prediction performance compared with CNN-based, CNN–GNN-based, and other surrogate models in terms of accuracy, stability, and uncertainty consistency. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Intelligent Enterprise Financial Management using Cognitive Digital Twin-Driven Financial Optimization Framework
Source title: 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Communication Systems, ICICACS 2026

Abstract: In recent years, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been integrated into enterprise financial management to improve decision-making under uncertain economic environments. This management has undergone significant transformation with increasing availability of large-scale financial data and complexity of global economic settings. Existing AI technique-based Research and Development (AIT-R&D) investment management models rely on static modeling and lack adaptive decision mechanisms, which limits their ability to capture dynamic financial dependencies and uncertainty. To address these limitations, this research proposes Cognitive Digital Twin-Driven Financial Optimization (CDT-FO) framework for intelligent enterprise financial management. Initially, this framework constructed financial digital twin to represent multi-dimensional financial states with internal financial variables and external market conditions. A graph-based cognitive model captures interdependencies between financial entities, while Transformer-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture to learn temporal dynamics. Bayesian modeling is incorporated for probabilistic risk estimation, and multi-objective optimization mechanism is employed to balance profit, risk, liquidity and cost under practical constraints. Finally, Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based decision module enables adaptive and feedback-driven financial strategy execution. The proposed CDT-FO framework demonstrates improved prediction accuracy of 0.98, with improved risk-aware decision-making as well as optimization performance compared to conventional methods. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: – Total vertical craniopagus represent one of the most complex craniofacial malformations and a demanding surgical challenge. Traditional imaging remains static and insufficient to fully anticipate dynamic venous redistribution during staged separation. We implemented an integrated virtual and physical simulation framework in the multistep separation of total vertical craniopagus twins, within an Avatar Patient Approach as an evolution of the Digital Twin Medicine approach focused on controlled physiological decoupling and operative risk reduction.METHODS: – Multimodal imaging Data sets were coregistered into a unified 3-dimensional anatomic space. These Data sets generated a dual avatar system: (1) immersive, multiuser virtual reality models within a collaborative metaverse; and (2) operable, multimaterial physical simulators enabling layered manual rehearsal. Both virtual and physical avatars were iteratively updated after each surgical stage, transforming simulation from a single preoperative event into a longitudinal adaptive workflow.RESULTS: – The integrated simulation reshaped the multistep approach, allowing venous partition strategies and refined cranial reconstruction planning to be discussed, replicated, and enhanced multidisciplinarily. Iterative model updating allowed anticipation of anatomic evolution between steps and facilitated scenario testing under alternative surgical hypotheses. Mental training was intended to support the development of 3-dimensional anatomic imagination, cognitive automatism, and surgical strategy definition. The platform helped reduce procedural uncertainty during planning and supported strategic decision-making.CONCLUSION: – Twin Medicine through dynamic virtual and physical avatars, redefines craniopagus separation surgery as a continuously adapting digital-physical continuum rather than a sequence of isolated operations. This paradigm establishes an iterative framework for managing extreme surgical complexity in pediatric neurosurgery. © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2026. All rights reserved.

Abstract: Membrane bioreactors (MBRs) are widely used in wastewater treatment, but fouling, energy demand, stringent effluent limits and nonlinear process behaviour still complicate routine operation. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods are increasingly reported for fouling prediction, process monitoring, soft sensing and operational optimisation in MBRs. For utility use, however, the question is less whether a model fits historical data than whether it can provide operators with reliable, interpretable and traceable information. Here, we assess AI-MBR research from that perspective. Direct AI-MBR evidence is separated from related membrane-process AI, broader wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) and water-AI evidence, and methodological studies on trustworthy AI. We also distinguish coded records from coded evidence occurrences, so that adjacent-domain studies are not read as evidence of MBR deployment. The literature shows a technical shift from early artificial neural network models for transmembrane-pressure prediction towards multimodal fouling diagnosis, uncertainty-aware prediction, digital-twin concepts and control-support studies. Evidence for deployment remains less mature. Recurring limitations include the lack of benchmark datasets, heterogeneous validation contexts, limited uncertainty quantification, weak cross-plant testing and incomplete audit and deployment reporting. Progress will depend on shared benchmark datasets, routine reporting of explanations and uncertainty, causal and transferable modelling, human-in-the-loop decision support and governance arrangements compatible with utility operation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Abstract: Digital twins integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) are emerging as key enablers for realizing net-zero energy systems. AI-enhanced digital twins improve the intelligence, efficiency, resilience, and sustainability of energy infrastructures through continuous monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent control of modern power systems. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in AI-based digital twin applications in the energy domain, focusing on system architectures, enabling AI methodologies, practical deployments, and cybersecurity challenges. Core AI techniques, including machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, federated learning, physics-informed models, and generative AI, are analyzed for grid optimization, predictive maintenance, renewable energy integration, and carbon-aware energy management. This paper examines security and trust issues through Zero-Trust architectures and governance frameworks for protecting critical energy infrastructures. Open research challenges such as scalability, data uncertainty, interoperability, model interpretability, and regulatory compliance are discussed to highlight existing research gaps. These insights guide future research and practical deployment of intelligent energy twins. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Decentralized Cooperative Power Dispatch Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Offline Digital Twin Technology for Building Integrated Photovoltaics and Energy Storage System Clusters

Abstract: Under carbon peaking and neutrality goals, building integrated with photovoltaics and energy storage system clusters (BIPECs) enable efficient on-site renewable energy use and can act as dispatch units for the public grid. However, BIPECs face significant uncertainties and are still under development. This study proposes a decentralized cooperative power dispatch model coupling a multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) algorithm and offline digital twin (ODT) technology to optimize the photovoltaic (PV) power consumption of clusters despite limited data availability. An integrated BIPEC energy system model is established, and by leveraging the multi-agent system model of the BIPEC, the decentralized dispatch problem is converted into a fully cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) problem. A simulation-assisted ODT framework constructs a digital environment for MAPPO to augment data, conduct MAPPO training, and optimize the reward function, thereby obtaining power dispatch strategies. The results show that the proposed optimization model can obtain dispatch strategies that reflect a high degree of collaboration, reducing the cumulative power supply from the public grid by 0.55–2.56% per month compared to the non-cooperative self-generating and self-using strategy. This study presents the application of MARL in BIPECs by introducing a decentralized collaborative power dispatch methodology for building clusters, enhancing building energy efficiency and facilitating flexible collaborative power dispatch. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: RhythmScheduler: Resilient TSN Scheduling under Temporal Uncertainty and Topology Churn
Affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China; Nio, Shanghai, China; Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou, China
Authors with affiliations: Wang K., University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China; Fu Z., University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China; Yan Y., University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China; Jia Y., Nio, Shanghai, China; Li W., Nio, Shanghai, China; Shen X., Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou, China; Li X.-Y., University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China
Abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) underpins time-critical industrial systems with ultra-low-latency, deterministic communication. However, long-term observations in real factories reveal that temporal uncertainty from legacy devices (jitter and clock drift) and topology churn from reconfigurable workflows break the assumptions of existing TSN schedulers, sharply degrading their performance. Therefore, we present RhythmScheduler, a fast, scalable TSN scheduler that explicitly models jitter and drift via three components: a temporal-stochastic graph encoder capturing timing variation and topology; a dual-head Transformer decoupling offset selection from guard-band allocation; and a Bayesian meta-adaptation loop on a hybrid digital twin, achieving sub-second reconfiguration with 3-4 ms inference. Extensive experiments on both simulation and hardware-in-the-loop testbeds show that RhythmScheduler improves schedulability by 12.2%/25.9%, reduces guard-band waste by 55.6%/62.6%, and generates Gate Control Lists (GCLs) 11.2×/14.8× faster on 200-link networks compared to state-of-the-art RL/heuristics-based methods; and achieves a further 52.9% schedulability gain, 52.5% waste reduction, and 10.9× speedup on 400-link networks, where prior RL baselines fail due to resource exhaustion. By combining efficiency with robustness, RhythmScheduler bridges deterministic TSN theory and noisy shop-floor reality, removing traffic scheduling as a bottleneck to agile industrial automation. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: CLAIR: SLA-Aware Inference Routing in Converged Cloud-Network Systems

Abstract: Deploying mission-critical AI services across converged cloud-network systems necessitates a delicate balance between diagnostic accuracy and service latency, a challenge exacerbated by stochastic network fluctuations. Existing offloading strategies typically rely on infrastructure-level metrics, often overlooking the intrinsic uncertainty of inference tasks and failing to strictly adhere to Service Level Agreements (SLAs). To bridge this gap, we propose CLAIR, a ConfidenceLatency Adaptive Inference Routing framework. CLAIR employs a confidence-gated mechanism that processes high-confidence, routine tasks at the edge while offloading ambiguous, lowconfidence samples to the cloud for expert reasoning. Crucially, to ensure SLA compliance under dynamic network conditions, we introduce Latency-Constrained Adaptive Thresholding (LCAT). This feedback-driven controller utilizes an AIMD-like strategy to dynamically modulate the offloading confidence threshold based on real-time latency observations. Experiments on a digital twin fault diagnosis testbed show that, in the evaluated setting, CLAIR achieves a more favorable accuracy-latency trade-off than stateof-the-art baselines. Quantitatively, the framework attains a steady-state accuracy of 88%-providing a 13% gain over pureedge execution-while reducing average end-to-end latency by 26% compared to queue-based heuristics, effectively preventing SLA violations during network congestion. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Reverse Variational Autoencoder: A probabilistic inference framework for structural health monitoring and inverse analysis in engineering
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China
Authors with affiliations: Zhao H.-Y., Department of Civil Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China; Wang C., Department of Civil Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China; Fan J.-S., Department of Civil Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China
Abstract: Inverse analysis in structural engineering involves inferring uncertain parameters from limited external observations, which is crucial for structural health monitoring and maintenance. However, real-world applications often face under-constrained problems with multiple possible solutions due to sparse measurements. This study proposes a Bayesian deep learning-based framework, termed Reverse Variational Auto-Encoder (RVAE), to fulfill efficient probabilistic structural inverse analysis. The RVAE framework modifies the original VAE structure to consider the causality relationship underlying inverse problems, enabling a semi-supervised learning paradigm for label-agnostic scenarios. The effectiveness of the RVAE framework is validated through a grid structure experiment. The implemented model successfully reveals all possible solutions for bending amplitudes, strains, and node displacements, with root-mean-squared reconstruction errors of 1.21 %, 2.77 %, and 1.36 %, respectively. A comparative analysis is conducted between mainstream inversion algorithms and RVAE. The results demonstrate that while all the other inversion algorithms achieve low reconstruction errors, they provide single-solution estimation, thus highlighting RVAE's capability to provide the most comprehensive information. RVAE's capability for real-time probabilistic estimation of structural parameters is further discussed and demonstrated in a full-scale bridge tower experiment, where it utilizes multi-sensor data to infer critical structural parameters, showing strong adaptability to noisy, incomplete, and heterogeneous monitoring inputs. In summary, RVAE tackles the challenges of large-scale parameter inversion in engineering structures by enabling efficient probabilistic inference under sparse observations. It supports semi-supervised learning in label-agnostic scenarios and real-time prediction of multiple plausible solutions, thereby fulfilling the synchronous updating requirements of digital twin systems. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A Digital-Twin-Aided Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Renewable-Integrated Residential Energy Management

Abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed renewable energy sources and electric vehicles (EVs) introduces significant operational challenges for residential energy management systems (HEMS), including stochastic renewable generation, uncertain load demand, device coupling, and physical safety constraints. This paper proposes a digital-twin-aided safe multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for coordinated energy management in renewable-integrated residential systems. The proposed approach models the battery energy storage system and the EV as independent agents and employs a multi-agent soft actor–critic (MASAC) algorithm with a centralised critic to capture the interactions among distributed energy resources. To improve decision quality under uncertainty, a digital twin module is developed to maintain a virtual representation of the residential energy system, synchronise operational states, update degradation-sensitive parameters, and generate short-term predictive information on photovoltaic (PV) generation and household load. The updated digital twin states and forecasts are incorporated into the observations of the reinforcement learning agents. In addition, a safety projection layer is incorporated to improve operational feasibility during both training and deployment. The environment considers realistic residential characteristics, including time-of-use electricity prices, battery degradation, EV mobility patterns, and grid energy trading. Simulation results show that the proposed framework reduces daily energy costs compared with rule-based baselines while maintaining EV charging reliability and operational feasibility. These results highlight the potential of combining predictive information, safety-constrained action execution, and multi-agent reinforcement learning for intelligent residential energy management. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Twintinuum: Advancing Self-Calibrating Physical-Digital Continuum
Affiliations: University of Amsterdam, Informatics Institute, Faculty of Science, Amsterdam, Netherlands
Authors with affiliations: Yang Z., University of Amsterdam, Informatics Institute, Faculty of Science, Amsterdam, Netherlands; Zhang X., University of Amsterdam, Informatics Institute, Faculty of Science, Amsterdam, Netherlands; Belloum A., University of Amsterdam, Informatics Institute, Faculty of Science, Amsterdam, Netherlands; Papagianni C., University of Amsterdam, Informatics Institute, Faculty of Science, Amsterdam, Netherlands; Grosso P., University of Amsterdam, Informatics Institute, Faculty of Science, Amsterdam, Netherlands
Abstract: Network Digital Twins (NDTs) are reshaping the network research landscape by enabling real-time predictive modeling and analysis of complex networked systems. Despite their potential, practical deployment of NDTs is hindered by growing divergence between the physical network and its digital replica, driven by insufficient or delayed synchronization, and the high communication overhead from continuous calibration, often worsened by inefficient data representation. To address these issues, we propose Twintinuum, a novel uncertainty-guided self-calibration mechanism that enables scalable twinning with low communication overhead. Our approach dynamically adapts the synchronization based on estimated model uncertainty, enabling both short-term responsiveness and long-term consistency. Moreover, the proposed framework supports plug-and-play calibration, allowing the digital twins to autonomously align with physical dynamics without extensive manual tuning or retraining. Extensive experiments on wireless signal datasets and diverse base models demonstrate that our method achieves superior signal quality estimation with significantly less data exchange. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: As a core component in steel production, the steel strip is prone to surface defects during the continuous production process due to its complex conditions. To achieve high-precision real-time monitoring of its surface quality and efficient quality control, the steel strip surface defect detection method is proposed based on uncertainty region fusion and digital twin (DT) model establishment. Specifically, the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) and Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) models pretrained on public defect datasets are used for independent surface detection, obtaining initial defect regions with confidence scores and uncertain detection results. To address single-model detection uncertainty and enhance detection accuracy, the decision-level uncertainty region fusion method is designed to fuse initial regions and uncertainty information based on region overlap and confidence, acquiring maximum reliable defect regions for surface defect recognition and localization. Different from existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) steel strip defect detection methods, the proposed method innovatively introduces uncertainty perception and diagonal equal-area decision-level fusion. It effectively reduces unreliable bounding box predictions and single-model detection bias and further realizes high-confidence defect data interaction and virtual–real synchronization with digital twin framework. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, the public datasets and experimental steel strip defect datasets are utilized with several defects. The results demonstrate that the proposed method yields consistent and significant improvements in detection accuracy, recall, and overlap rate on both the public Northeastern University (NEU) dataset and the self-built dataset, which verifies the value for steel strip quality control and intelligent manufacturing. Abstract: Ultra–low-noise inertial sensors are a cornerstone of modern geoscientific instrumentation, enabling high-resolution observations across seismology, geodesy, gravimetry, and vibration isolation. Achieving and reliably predicting their performance requires a rigorous treatment of physical causality, noise propagation, and uncertainty, particularly in force-feedback architectures operating near fundamental limits. In this study, we introduce a causal and uncertainty-aware digital-twin framework for the design and metrological assessment of ultra–low-noise geoscientific inertial sensors. The proposed framework integrates mechanical dynamics, force-feedback control, transduction, and digital acquisition within a physically realisable model that explicitly enforces causality and stability constraints. Starting from a minimal equation-of-motion description, the digital twin is formulated in the frequency domain to construct causal transfer functions and a comprehensive noise-budget model. The framework enables the systematic separation of fundamental thermal noise limits from implementation-dependent noise sources, including readout, actuation, and digital acquisition effects. We introduce quantitative performance metrics based on self-noise spectra, dominant noise regimes, crossover frequencies, and nearplateau bandwidths, allowing complex spectral behaviour to be condensed into actionable design indicators. Parameter uncertainties are propagated through the digital twin to provide uncertainty-aware performance estimates and robustness diagnostics. Through a series of illustrative analyses, we demonstrate how the proposed digital twin supports informed design trade-offs, identifies performance bottlenecks, and prevents non-physical or overly optimistic sensitivity estimates arising from non-causal modelling assumptions. While focused on inertial sensors, the methodology is general and transferable to other classes of geoscientific instruments. The framework provides a transparent and extensible foundation for next-generation sensor design, virtual experimentation, and metrologically consistent performance prediction. © 2026 Antonino D'Alessandro.

Title: Dynamic Hierarchical Posterior Evolution for Bayesian Neural Network-Based Industrial Digital Twins under Non-Stationary Conditions

Abstract: Industrial digital twins must continuously ingest online data during long-term operation and revise the virtual-to-physical mapping under non-stationary factors such as operating-condition switching, equipment degradation, and observation bias. Conventional deterministic models cannot explicitly characterize predictive uncertainty, while existing Bayesian continual-learning methods still suffer from weak historical knowledge retention, limited physical-consistency constraints, and degraded uncertainty quality under drift. To address these issues, this paper proposes Dynamic Hierarchical Posterior Evolution (DHPE) for non-stationary industrial digital twins. In the representation layer, a hierarchical Gaussian-Inv-Gamma formulation with dynamic scale adjustment is introduced to maintain uncertainty health during online updating. In the evolution layer, complex posteriors are projected into Gaussian-mixture interface posteriors, and geometric Wasserstein distance is used to jointly incorporate historical posterior inheritance and physically anchored priors, thereby enabling smooth recursion under non-Gaussian conditions while preserving long-term physical consistency. A closed-loop mechanism integrating drift monitoring, state switching, and geometric feedback is further constructed to adaptively regulate inheritance strength, anchoring stiffness, and uncertainty width. Online experiments on titanium reduction furnace temperature prediction under three representative non-stationary scenarios show that DHPE delivers more stable error trajectories, more reasonable interval coverage, and more consistent probabilistic predictions, while maintaining strong posterior recovery capability and long-term robustness. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Noise-robust knowledge distillation for industrial digital twins

Abstract: Recent advances in Knowledge Distillation (KD) have highlighted the importance of decoupling target and non-target class knowledge. However, in complex scenarios such as industrial digital twins, input data is frequently corrupted by random noise due to electromagnetic interference or sensor aging. While existing fixed-weight distillation strategies perform well on clean data, they exhibit severe vulnerabilities in noisy environments: when the input image is perturbed, the teacher network's predictions for non-target classes contain substantial random fluctuations. Maintaining a high weight for these predictions forces the student network to mimic meaningless noise patterns, leading to significant performance degradation.To overcome this limitation, we propose Adaptive Noise-Aware Knowledge Distillation (ANA-KD), a parameter-free, bidirectional dynamic weight adjustment framework tailored for noisy industrial environments. First, we introduce an information entropy-based noise perception mechanism that quantifies the pollution level of the current sample by measuring the uncertainty in the teacher network's predictive probability distribution. Furthermore, we propose a "scissors-like"bidirectional adaptive weighting strategy. Upon detecting high-noise inputs, the algorithm dynamically reduces the weight β to actively filter out corrupted detailed dark knowledge, while simultaneously increasing the weight α to guide the student network to focus on robust backbone structural features. Extensive experiments across varying noise intensities and network architectures on CIFAR-100 demonstrate the effectiveness of ANA-KD. Particularly under severe noise interference, the proposed algorithm exhibits exceptional defense capabilities without introducing any additional convolutional parameters, ensuring high efficiency for edge deployment. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Quantum-Inspired Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Semiconductor Wafer Probing in Multi-Die Environments

Affiliations: NXP Semiconductors San Jose, CA, United States
Authors with affiliations: Gondi S.R., NXP Semiconductors San Jose, CA, United States
Abstract: It has been suggested in the present paper that a Quantum-Inspired Reinforcement Learning (QIRL) framework can be proposed to adaptive semiconductor wafer probing in intricate multi-die settings, where traditional deterministic policies and classical reinforcement learning frameworks have difficulties in combinatorial explosion, sparse reward gradients, and uneven distributions of defects. The proposed approach introduces an amplitude-based superposition mechanism for probabilistic policy encoding, enabling the simultaneous exploration of multiple probing trajectories and improving decision-making efficiency under uncertainty. The environment of the high-fidelity digital twin simulation was created based on the realistic conditions of the wafer, which included the heterogeneous die layout, stochastic defect patterns (random, clustered and edge-based), and probe degradation dynamics. QIRL framework was strictly tested with comparison to the baseline procedures that were deterministic raster scanning, tabular Q-learning, Deep Q-Network (DQN), and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The effectiveness of the proposed model is shown to be reduced to 28 % less probing moves than raster scanning and 17 % less than classical Q-learning through experimentation. Also, the switching costs are minimized up to 22% compared to PPO, which means an increase in the efficiency of path optimization. QIRL has a defect detection accuracy of 94/97 on average with a false positive rate of less than 3 meaning that in clustered defect situations, QIRL is able to find defects with a high accuracy of up to 97. Moreover, the framework also decreases the wear of probes by about 20 %, which leads to the increased lifespan of the equipment and reliability of the testing. All in all, the presented QIRL model is an excellent balance between the probing efficiency, accuracy of defect localization, and hardware durability. The findings indicate that it is scalable and can be used in next-generation semiconductor testing, and its potential is high when it comes to implementation in hybrid quantum-classical computing systems. © 2026, Innovative Information Science and Technology Research Group. Title: Uncertainty-aware temperature field reconstruction from sparse samples and sensing via latent-space enhancement for GIS digital twin applications

Abstract: Efficient and reliable full-state temperature estimation is critical for condition monitoring and digital twin applications of enclosed high-voltage equipment, yet it remains challenging due to sparse measurements and the high computational cost of multiphysics simulations. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware workflow for full-state temperature estimation of a 550 kV gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) disconnector under contact degradation scenarios, based on a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) reduced-order representation. A probabilistic forward surrogate enables posterior-driven data augmentation, while a lightweight inverse surrogate is trained to infer POD coefficients from only three temperature measurements on the enclosure surface, followed by full-state reconstruction with uncertainty quantification. Numerical results on the evaluated cases show favorable reconstruction accuracy and noise tolerance, with lower errors than gappy POD under the reported settings despite using fewer sensors. These results indicate the potential of the proposed workflow for digital twin-oriented temperature-field estimation in GIS. © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: Background Climate change and agricultural intensification have made light limitation a key constraint on crop light use efficiency and yield potential. Research has progressed from description to quantification, mechanistic understanding, and multiscale modeling. However, indicator systems remain fragmented, and cross-scale integration is weak. These gaps limit translation to breeding and on-farm practice. Aim of review This review integrates the multidimensional networks and key strategies of crop adaptation to light limitation. It identifies core methodological bottlenecks that hinder prediction and application. It proposes a forward-looking paradigm to support mechanistic insight, breeding for shade efficiency, and precision management under complex light environments. Key scientific concepts of review Crop adaptation to light limitation arises from coordinated networks of light signaling, metabolic regulation, and architectural optimization. Two strategic modes dominate: shade avoidance and shade tolerance. C3 and C4 species show distinct response logic due to differences in energetics, anatomy, and regulatory control. Progress is constrained by the absence of a unified, cross-scale indicator framework and by bottlenecks in model prediction and scale coupling. This review proposes an integrated systems-biology approach enabled by high-throughput phenotyping and artificial intelligence for science. The framework standardizes indicators and fuses multimodal data across scales. It further links data assimilation with physics-informed learning to build multiscale digital twins. This approach reduces indicator fragmentation, strengthens cross-scale coupling, and supports uncertainty-aware decisions and breeding targets for shade-efficient cultivars. It opens a path to quantitative prediction and actionable management of crop performance under complex light regimes. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Walczak K.; Bergés M.
Author full names: Walczak, Krzysztof (60739986100); Bergés, Mario (26326769400)
Title: Exploring LLM-Powered Agents for Modeling Thermal Dynamics of Buildings
Source title: Proceedings of the 13th ACM International Conference on Systems for Energy-Efficient Buildings, Cities, and Transportation, BuildSys 2026
Affiliations: Amazon, Seattle, WA, United States; Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, United States
Authors with affiliations: Walczak K., Amazon, Seattle, WA, United States; Bergés M., Amazon, Seattle, WA, United States, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, United States
Abstract: Modeling building thermal dynamics is essential for energy optimization, yet building heterogeneity and non-stationary dynamics demand per-building customization that typically requires expert intervention. Automated scientific discovery workflows powered by Large Language Models (LLM) could significantly decrease the human expertise requirements for generating custom thermal models at scale, but their performance varies considerably depending on configuration and task, raising a key question: how should we configure scientific agents for thermal dynamics modeling? To answer this, we developed ThermalForge1, a platform for experimenting with agentic approaches to hybrid neural-physics modeling of thermal dynamics. Using a year-long dataset from hundreds of U.S. residential smart thermostats, we investigate the impact of physics knowledge in prompts, constraints on neural architecture search, LLM effectiveness in determining physics-neural transition points, model stochasticity, cost-accuracy tradeoffs, and performance against benchmark methods. Our results show that agentic modeling can match or exceed state-of-the-art automated methods while offering greater flexibility and reduced expertise requirements. We found important differences in configuring the physics-neural transition point, and demonstrate how the inherent variability of LLM outputs can be transformed from uncertainty into a mechanism for robust model discovery. This work presents the first large-scale application of LLM-powered modeling agents to real-world observational data, demonstrating their viability for thermal dynamics modeling and paving the way to scalable methods that embed domain expertise within automated workflows. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

Title: Opportunities and Credibility Challenges of Generative AI-Enhanced Digital Twins Across Science and Engineering

Abstract: Digital twins (DTs) have emerged as an important paradigm across science, engineering, healthcare, and medicine. This review examines generative AI (GenAI)-based data-driven DTs across soil science, wearable sensors, materials science, and precision medicine. We compare where GenAI-enhanced DT workflows show promise and where important limitations remain. We emphasize the critical role of verification and validation and uncertainty quantification, as well as definitional clarity and the distinction between statistical realism and scientific validity. These workflows can help address sparse data, accelerate analysis, and support decision-making, but predictive performance alone does not establish that a GenAI-enhanced DT is credible, interpretable, or fit for decision support. © 1999-2011 IEEE.

Title: A probabilistic digital twin framework for corrosion-fatigue prognosis of floating offshore wind turbines

Abstract: Floating offshore wind turbines face growing integrity-management challenges caused by coupled corrosion and fatigue in harsh marine environments. Existing digital-twin frameworks are not yet well suited to combine multi-phase degradation physics with dynamic uncertainty quantification for this problem. To address this gap, this paper proposes a probabilistic digital twin framework that integrates sensor data acquisition, multi-physics simulation, and Bayesian inference for corrosion-fatigue prognosis. A three-phase damage evolution model is formulated to represent the transition from corrosion pitting to short-crack growth and long-crack propagation. Operational observations are assimilated recursively to update fatigue parameters and remaining useful life estimates. The framework is demonstrated using the IEA 15 MW reference wind turbine. The updated model identifies the onset of accelerated crack propagation at year 20 and reduces the 95% remaining-useful-life confidence interval from 40.4 years to 3.4 years. A maintenance strategy based on the updated failure probability reduces operational downtime by 58% and lifecycle cost by approximately 64.9% compared with a fixed-interval strategy. The results indicate that probabilistic updating can support more transparent inspection and maintenance decisions for floating offshore wind turbine structures under corrosion-fatigue degradation. © 2026 by the authors.

Abstract: Modern supply chains face high uncertainty and demand for speed. AI enables a shift from reactive to proactive management, evolving from expert systems and basic ML to deep learning, reinforcement learning, and hybrid models. Key applications include demand forecasting, transport logistics optimization, and predictive inventory management. AI with blockchain ensures transparency and smart contracts. Strengths are accuracy and adaptability; weaknesses include high complexity, data dependence, and poor interpretability. Barriers are poor data quality, low digital maturity, staff resistance, skill shortages, and integration issues. Solutions involve unified data spaces, cloud platforms, and phased pilots. Trends include digital twins, autonomous systems, and Green AI. Recommendations aim to boost sustainability and cost-efficiency. © 2027 by IGI Global Scientific Publishing. All rights reserved.

Abstract: As the global energy sector seeks to reduce dependence on fossil fuel–based generation and mitigate carbon emissions, there is an increasing need to evaluate advanced enabling platforms that support sustainable energy integration. Technologies, such as digital twin (DT) and virtual power plant (VPP), provide enhanced capabilities for detailed modeling, monitoring, and optimization of modern power systems with high penetration of renewable energy sources (RESs). This study proposes an integrated DT–VPP framework for effective management of distributed energy resources (DERs), particularly photovoltaic (PV) systems, while also presenting a wind turbine (WT) simulation case using distributionally robust optimization (DRO) to improve grid stability under uncertainty. The proposed framework enables real-time asset monitoring, operational optimization, and enhanced decision-making to mitigate technical constraints such as power losses, capacity limitations, and renewable intermittency. Furthermore, the study highlights the role of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven strategies in improving predictive analytics, system reliability, and resilience of future smart grids. The findings demonstrate that the integration of DT, VPP, and AI-based optimization techniques can significantly enhance grid stability, operational flexibility, and sustainable energy management. Title: Human Factors of Quantum Modeling and Computing
Source title: Communications in Computer and Information Science
Affiliations: Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47907, IN, United States
Authors with affiliations: Liu P., Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47907, IN, United States; Yu D., Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47907, IN, United States
Abstract: Quantum mechanics and computing has potential for advancing human factors and ergonomics (HFE) research by providing novel theories and methods for modeling cognition and human-centered systems. This paper presents a comprehensive review of quantum modeling and computing within HFE on both theory and application. This review first discuss quantum cognition, where the uncertainty principle and quantum probability theory refines models of human decision-making under uncertainty. Building on these foundations, the review discusses human–computer interaction (HCI) on quantum systems, demonstrating current challenges in usability. The concept of quantum digital twins (QDTs) is introduced as an extension of digital twin technology, integrating human centric data for real-time healthcare. Finally, the paper surveys the role of quantum artificial intelligence (QAI) in augmenting human work and analyzing human-centric data with potential for computational acceleration and improved predictive performance. Together, these advances illustrate a bidirectional pathway, HCI drive innovations in quantum technologies while integrating quantum frameworks into reshapes cognitive models along with expanding human-centered AI, and human digital twin. This review establishes a conceptual baseline for future interdisciplinary research of quantum science and HFE. 150–250 words. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

Title: Learning Ocean Channel Cartography: A Digital Twin Approach to Communication-Aware Autonomy for Maritime 6G
Affiliations: University of Iceland, Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Reykjavik, 102, Iceland; Marine and Fresh Water Research Institute, Hafnarfjörur, 220, Iceland; Reykjavik University, Department of Applied Engineering, Reykjavik, 102, Iceland
Authors with affiliations: Mahgoli M., University of Iceland, Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Reykjavik, 102, Iceland; Akyildiz I.F., University of Iceland, Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Reykjavik, 102, Iceland; Andersen K., University of Iceland, Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Reykjavik, 102, Iceland; Sofia Giesta Da Silva T., Marine and Fresh Water Research Institute, Hafnarfjörur, 220, Iceland; Thorsteinsson S.E., Reykjavik University, Department of Applied Engineering, Reykjavik, 102, Iceland
Abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) swarms are fundamentally constrained by communication channels whose quality varies sharply with position and depth. Conventional path planning treats connectivity as a reactive constraint, causing mission failures when vehicles encounter dead zones from multipath fading, thermal stratification, or acoustic shadowing. This paper presents Ocean Channel Cartography (OCC), a framework that constructs persistent 3D channel quality maps via cooperative sensing and Gaussian Process (GP) interpolation with an oceanographically-structured composite kernel. Contributions include: 1) a composite GP kernel combining squared-exponential, periodic, and Matérn components to encode large-scale stratification, thermocline-related vertical periodicity, and bathymetric irregularities; 2) a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) controller jointly optimizing mission coverage, communication reliability, and energy through uncertainty-aware rewards; 3) an adaptive multi-modal switching mechanism for acoustic, Magnetic Induction, and optical transceivers; and 4) a collaborative multi-mission learning protocol refining a shared, persistent map across deployments. Relative to an acoustic-only baseline, the multi-modal scheme yields an aggregate throughput gain of 3.87×± 0.21× through spatial offloading. Monte Carlo simulations show that the composite GP kernel reduces channel-map RMSE to 2.65 dB versus 3.52 dB (SE-only) and 3.57 dB (Matérn-only) averaged across eight environments (a ≈25 reduction), with the largest environment-specific gain reaching 3.3× in thermocline-dominated regimes. Under the simulated evaluation setting, the hierarchical DRL controller retained 48.2% of the initial energy budget compared with 9.9% for a Flat MARL baseline (Table III), at 82.4% vs. 86.4% mission progress. Multi-mission learning across three environments improves mission completion from 36.0% to 70.0%. These results suggest OCC as a direction worth further study for maritime 6G, with field validation identified as the essential next step.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: AI Augmented Synthetic CT Framework for Pulmonary Nodule Analysis and Uncertainty-aware Treatment Response Prediction in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
Source title: International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems
Affiliations: Department of Networking and Communications, School of Computing, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Kattankulathur, Tamilnadu, Chennai, 603203, India
Authors with affiliations: Poornima G., Department of Networking and Communications, School of Computing, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Kattankulathur, Tamilnadu, Chennai, 603203, India; Anand L., Department of Networking and Communications, School of Computing, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Kattankulathur, Tamilnadu, Chennai, 603203, India
Abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, with early detection hampered by rare nodule morphologies and a persistent shortage of annotated training data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an anatomy-informed digital twin framework, referred to as LungSimNet4D, that integrates anatomy-aware thoracic phantoms, procedural lesion embedding, and GATE CT simulation to construct LungSimNet4D Dataset — a synthetic dataset of 1,044 CT volumes covering nodule diameters from 4 to 30 mm across solid, part-solid, and ground-glass morphologies, consistent with NLST population distributions. The proposed system achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.92 for nodule segmentation using nnU-Net, a detection AUC of 0.95 and classification AUC of 0.94 using MONAI ResNet-3D on LUNA16 and DLCSD24 benchmarks — corresponding to improvements of 10 percentage points over the non-augmented baseline and 6–7 percentage points over recently published methods in detection and segmentation accuracy. For treatment-response prediction, the framework achieved an RMSE of approximately 5% of observed tumour volume change through Monte Carlo-based Verification, Validation and Uncertainty Quantification (VVUQ), with anti-EGFR therapy simulations yielding a mean tumour volume reduction of 45% (95% CI: 32–58%) — a 37.5% RMSE reduction (from 8% to 5%) compared to static baseline models. Ablation studies confirmed that each component — synthetic augmentation, anatomy-constrained phantom modelling, and uncertainty quantification — contributes independently to overall performance. The framework demonstrates a scalable, computationally validated, and reproducible digital twin platform for NSCLC research, supporting privacy-preserving multi-institutional deployment through federated learning and establishing a rigorous foundation for precision oncology workflows, pending prospective clinical validation. Title: Designing a Local Digital Twin for Port-City Energy Systems: Coupling Urban Building Energy Modeling with a Lightweight Onshore Power Supply Port Module and Urban Electrification Hooks

Abstract: Ports are electrifying through onshore power supply (OPS) while adjacent urban districts electrify heat and mobility, creating coupled peak-demand risks at shared distributiongrid boundaries. Yet port and city energy systems are often assessed in silos, limiting the ability to quantify coincident peaks, grid headroom, and the value of coordinated flexibility. This paper presents a Digital Twin-ready, decision-oriented coupling workflow that links an Urban Building Energy Model (UBEM) with a lightweight port energy module focused on OPS through a data-minimal coupling contract and an explicit orchestration layer. The contribution is framed as an early-stage screening architecture, rather than a fully operational Digital Twin, for translating simultaneous port-city electrification into feasibility indicators under shared local grid constraints. Uncertainty hooks (OPS uptake, electric vehicle (EV) / heat pump (HP) overlays, and assumed headroom) enable scenario stress-testing without changing the core modules. An executable illustrative workflow using a district UBEM profile and a synthetic OPS generator produces feasibility-driven planning outputs, including congestion exposure, OPS energy served versus reduced under peak management, and an OPS supportability frontier across headroom caps.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Research on Supply Chain Resilience Assessment Model Based on Digital Twin and IoT
Source title: Conference Proceedings - CNIOT 2026: 2026 7th International Conference on Computing, Networks and Internet of Things
Affiliations: Chongqing Jiaotong University, Chongqing, China
Authors with affiliations: Zhou W., Chongqing Jiaotong University, Chongqing, China
Abstract: Supply chain disruptions caused by demand fluctuations and supply uncertainties pose significant challenges to traditional supply chain systems. Conventional decision-making approaches often rely on static information and lack real-time responsiveness, resulting in poor adaptability under sudden shocks. To address this issue, this paper proposes a supply chain resilience evaluation framework based on Digital Twin and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies. A dynamic inventory model is constructed to simulate a three-echelon supply chain system under stochastic demand and disruption scenarios. Two operational modes, namely a traditional static policy and a digital twin-driven dynamic policy, are compared through discrete-time simulation. The results show that, compared with the traditional system, the digital twin-enabled approach reduces inventory fluctuation by approximately 45%-55%, decreases shortage levels by over 90%, and improves recovery speed by around 40% under disruption scenarios. These findings demonstrate that integrating real-time data and virtual simulation significantly enhances supply chain resilience by enabling proactive and adaptive decision-making. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Dataset on the reproducibility of UHPC mechanical properties under a fixed recipe with controlled production variability
Affiliations: Department of Measurement and Control Engineering, University of Kassel, Kassel, Germany; QuantumFusion GmbH, Kassel, Germany; MAITERIA UG, Kassel, Germany
Authors with affiliations: Rezazadeh F., Department of Measurement and Control Engineering, University of Kassel, Kassel, Germany; Abrishambaf A., QuantumFusion GmbH, Kassel, Germany; Zimmermann G., MAITERIA UG, Kassel, Germany; Kroll A., Department of Measurement and Control Engineering, University of Kassel, Kassel, Germany
Abstract: A dataset was collected to investigate the reproducibility of ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC) quality under controlled variability, since UHPC mechanical properties can vary even when using a fixed mix formulation in production. This dataset is the first open-access dataset in the UHPC community to take a holistic view of the UHPC production process and associated production variability, featuring a relatively large number of systematically designed experiments under a fixed recipe. A reference UHPC recipe, designed for a 28-day compressive strength of 120 MPa, was used to produce 150 experimental records, while the quality, storage conditions, and dosing accuracy of raw materials, along with mixing parameters and curing conditions, were systematically varied to emulate real-world production environments. For each batch, five fresh UHPC properties and the average mixer power were recorded, and compressive and flexural strengths at 24 hours and at 28 days were measured using standardized methods under controlled laboratory conditions. By linking process variability to mechanical outcomes under the fixed reference recipe, the dataset supports reproducibility analysis in UHPC production and provides reusable data for machine learning, uncertainty modeling, and digital-twin development. © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: The concept of structural health monitoring (SHM) of civil infrastructure has evolved rapidly with the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI). Although available literature mainly focuses on supervised and unsupervised learning to detect and classify damages, both are inherently limited in addressing sequential decision-making, optimization of long-term maintenance, adaptive sensing, and dynamic uncertainty handling. In comparison, reinforcement learning (RL) offers a policy-based framework that can learn optimal actions by interacting with changing structural and environmental circumstances. Although there is an increasing use of RL applications in SHM, there has not been a comprehensive and critical review of RL applications. This review paper critically evaluates RL approaches used in civil infrastructure SHM, which spans across sensor network optimization, energy management of internet of things (IoT)–based wireless sensor networks (WSNs), updating finite element models (FEMs), contact and noncontact damage detection, unmanned vehicle-based inspection, predictive maintenance planning, autonomous SHM and structural control, etc. The review traces the methodological development from tabular Q-learning to complex deep reinforcement learning (DRL), multiagent systems, hierarchical designs, and combined physics-informed systems. In each of these areas, RL shows a high potential in adaptive resource scheduling, enhanced damage localization, large-scale network maintenance planning, integration of digital twins, federated learning, edge intelligence, and smart infrastructure ecosystems. Nevertheless, a few inherent challenges that prevent large-scale applications, such as high-dimensional state-action spaces, complexity in reward engineering, sample inefficiency, lack of real-world validation, and lack of transferability to heterogeneous infrastructure types, are discussed. Most of the existing implementations are simulation-based or applied to lab-scale models and lack standardized validation procedures for field deployment. Future research should focus on physics-informed and risk-sensitive formulations of RL in safety-critical systems, as well as on scalable multiagent and hierarchical learning designs, transfer and federated learning to alleviate data scarcity and privacy limitations, uncertainty-aware safe exploration strategies, and enhanced interchangeability with IoT-enabled digital twin ecosystems. Through this review, academicians, researchers and industrial experts will get critical insights on RL-based SHM to transform into an intelligent, resilient, sustainable, and autonomous infrastructure monitoring. Abstract: Multiscale damage modeling of fiber reinforced composites (FRCs) is a central scientific issue for ensuring their service reliability in critical engineering fields such as aerospace and advanced equipment. This review systematically reviews recent advances in multiscale modeling techniques for FRCs damage simulation, with the aim of clarifying the underlying logic, coupling mechanisms, and development trends of different modeling strategies, thereby providing a theoretical support for next generation high fidelity predictive systems. This work firstly elaborates the fundamental theories of multiscale modeling, summarizes the evolution paths of cross-scale damage and classical failure criteria, and clarifies the carrier function of representative volume element (RVE) in cross-scale information transmission. Subsequently, a critical evaluation is conducted on various mainstream modeling strategies to reveal their essential distinctions and complementary scopes between mechanism-oriented and efficiency-oriented paradigms. Furthermore, hierarchical validation strategies for multiscale modeling are discussed. Combined with sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification techniques, an evaluation framework ranging from single-scale self-consistency to full-scale closed-loop assessment is established. Finally, current research challenges are analyzed, and four major frontier directions are identified: dynamic mapping between manufacturing defects and service performance, construction of multiscale multiphysics coupled models, deep integration of physics and data-driven modeling, and closed loop evolution of digital twins. This review is intended to provide a systematic and forward looking perspective for future research in this field and to promote the development of multiscale damage models for FRCs with higher computational efficiency and stronger predictive capability. © 2026

Title: AI Enabled Digital Twin Framework for Renewable Integrated Electric Vehicle Charging and V2G Systems

Abstract: The increasing penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) and renewable energy sources introduces significant challenges for power system operation due to variability, uncertainty, and growing peak demand. This paper proposes an AI-enabled digital twin framework for renewable-integrated EV charging infrastructure with vehicle to grid (V2G) capability. The framework establishes a cyber-physical replica of the charging system that continuously synchronizes with physical assets to enable predictive monitoring, forecasting, and intelligent control. Machine learning models are employed to forecast renewable generation and EV charging demand, while an optimization-based energy management strategy coordinates bidirectional power exchange among renewable sources, EV batteries, and the utility grid. Simulation-based case studies demonstrate improved renewable energy utilization, reduced grid dependency, and lower charging costs compared with conventional uncoordinated charging strategies. The results confirm that integrating artificial intelligence with digital twin technology provides a scalable and adaptive solution for sustainable transportation and smart energy systems. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Verification of digital twins, especially in the presence of distributed components and asynchronous communication, remains a fundamental challenge. Uncertainty arises not only from the physical environment and virtual representations, but also from the bidirectional flow of data between them. This paper presents a formal verification methodology that captures these dynamics by translating a digital twin’s probabilistic elements into a finite state machine, augmented with explicit models of message delay and concurrent evolution. Using the Temporal Logic of Actions (TLA), we specify and verify temporal properties that ensure system-level correctness despite communication disorder and component-level asynchrony. We demonstrate this approach on a digital twin of an unmanned aerial vehicle, showing how to verify synchronization properties that govern end-to-end coherence between the physical and virtual components. Our case study highlights how formal specification clarifies system modeling choices, including which guarantees must hold, how system behaviors should be represented, and what assumptions are essential. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated the advancement of autonomous systems by enabling higher levels of automated decision-making and control. In the maritime sector, autonomous ships are increasingly regarded as an important future direction for shipping. This study reviews current approaches to software safety and investigates how AI-related risks are addressed in autonomous-system development across different industries, with particular attention to autonomous ships. Following the PRISMA guidelines, 389 research articles from the Web of Science Core Collection and 76 AI-related incident reports from transportation industries were analysed. In addition, 11 maritime regulatory and classification society guidelines were evaluated using a structured qualitative coding scheme to examine software safety and AI-specific provisions. The review identifies several challenges associated with AI-driven systems, including adversarial attacks, tail-risk scenarios, limited causal understanding, and uncertainty in decision-making. Existing maritime frameworks remain insufficient in software reliability, verification, validation, and uncertainty-aware risk management for complex operational environments. Comparisons with the automotive and other transportation sectors highlight the need for adaptive stress testing, scenario-based simulation, formal verification, digital twins, and AI-specific risk assessment methods to improve the resilience and reliability of AI-driven autonomous ship systems. © 2026 Institute of Marine Engineering, Science & Technology.

Authors: Tai C.; Guo J.; Li C.; Fattahi J.
Title: Digital twin-in-the-loop energy management for grid-edge flexibility in electrified residential buildings
Affiliations: SWTCH Energy Inc., Toronto, Canada; School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Ottawa, Ottawa, Canada
Authors with affiliations: Tai C., SWTCH Energy Inc., Toronto, Canada; Guo J., SWTCH Energy Inc., Toronto, Canada; Li C., SWTCH Energy Inc., Toronto, Canada; Fattahi J., School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Ottawa, Ottawa, Canada
Abstract: We present an integrated framework for coordinating residential electrified loads in multi-unit residential buildings (MURBs) using heat-pump digital twins in the loop (DTiL), reinforcement learning (RL), and Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (DRO). The framework is designed to support MURBs as flexible grid-edge resources under uncertain and stressed operating conditions, including weather-driven demand variability. The heat-pump DTiL combines a reduced-order thermal balance, a coefficient-of-performance (COP) power map, and a learned disturbance channel and is synchronized with streaming telemetry through an event-aware observer to produce horizon forecasts of heat-pump electrical demand. These local short-horizon predictions are used alongside an RL policy that proposes EVSE charging schedules, after which a tractable convex DRO reformulation is used to obtain schedules that remain feasible under uncertainty in non-EV demand and EV availability while satisfying sub-feeder and main-panel ampacity limits. The DTiL framework couples online demand prediction with robust schedule correction, allowing the controller to adapt to time-varying building conditions without relying solely on nominal forecasts. Experiments quantify DT prediction accuracy, robust scheduling feasibility, and reliability–utilization trade-offs under weather-sensitive load variation. In an 8-unit residential pilot, the approach achieved electrical-power error of 35.9-45.3 W and scheduling efficiency of 91% across robustness settings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Digital twins in geotechnical engineering: bridging data, models, and engineering practice
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad, Jharkhand, Dhanbad, India
Authors with affiliations: Tiwari S., Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad, Jharkhand, Dhanbad, India; Das S.K., Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad, Jharkhand, Dhanbad, India
Abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) have brought rapid transformation in several engineering sectors; however, their application in geotechnical engineering remains limited due to the challenges related to real-time data integration, complexity of computation, standardisation issues, and immature technology. This study evaluates the current state of adoption of DTs in geotechnical engineering and proposes a comprehensive application-oriented workflow approach for creating a geotechnical DT. The research trends, technological advancements, and application domains were assessed using bibliometric analysis and an extensive literature survey. The findings of the study indicate that the application of DTs in the geotechnical field falls largely in low to mid technological readiness levels (TRL of 1 to 5), with most of the studies falling in the category of digital shadow or having limited DT implementations. A significant research need concerning uncertainty propagation, data interoperability, sensor reliability, cybersecurity, and field-scale application is identified by this study. Based on these findings, the study proposes a methodological framework that integrates real-time sensing networks, communication protocols, artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML)-based surrogate models, and data-driven and physics-informed decision-making for geotechnical assets monitoring and management. This study broadens the possible uses of DTs in problems, such as real-time slope deformation monitoring, tunnels and underground space planning, liquefaction hazard assessment, performance-based assessment of dams, embankments, foundations, etc. The article emphasises the limited research and utilisation of DTs while addressing the extensive opportunities for future development. It calls for action from researchers and industry professionals to explore the untapped potential of DTs in geotechnical engineering. © Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Abstract: Accurate furnace-roof temperature prediction is critical for energy-efficient reheating-furnace operation, refractory safety assessment, and cleaner production. However, nonlinear radiation–conduction–convection coupling, multilayer refractory interfaces, heterogeneous boundary conditions, and real-time inference requirements remain difficult to reconcile using conventional numerical or purely data-driven models. This study proposes a multidimensional digital-twin framework for thermo-mechanical coupled modelling of a 2250 walking-beam reheating furnace. The framework couples geometric, thermal, and stress surrogate models with an application-specific Generalized Physics-Informed Neural Network (G-PINN). G-PINN integrates finite-element shape-function-based derivative evaluation, nodal degree-of-freedom assignment for prescribed Dirichlet boundaries, and Gaussian-quadrature-based energy-functional loss within a unified furnace-roof modelling pipeline. Under synchronized quasi-steady validation, the fixed trained model independently maps each time-indexed boundary-condition vector to its corresponding temperature field without online retraining. In Heating Zone II, G-PINN achieves an MAE of 2.3–3.2 °C and an R2 of 0.920–0.942, reducing RMSE by approximately 40–50% relative to the steady-state FEM reference. The full framework obtains a mean MAE of 2.75 °C, satisfies prescribed Dirichlet boundaries exactly, and completes end-to-end temperature prediction, gradient evaluation, stress computation, and von Mises post-processing within 8.2 ms. FEM-referenced stress assessment indicates that operational stresses remain below 13 MPa in structurally active regions, while first-order heat-loss sensitivity analysis suggests a 0.64–2.18% uncertainty-bounded potential reduction in redundant heat loss. These results support real-time quasi-steady furnace-roof temperature prediction, stress assessment, and cleaner-operation decision support, while transient thermal inertia remains outside the present validation scope. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Abstract: To address the conflict between physical fidelity and computational efficiency in vehicle-to-grid applications, this paper proposes a mechanism-data hybrid digital twin framework for reversible solid oxide cells. A quasi-two-dimensional dynamic model is developed using the control volume method to describe the axial multi-physics coupling. Crucially, to overcome the high computational burden of nonlinear node current solution in distributed models, which limits real-time execution, a PID-modulated current allocation algorithm is introduced into the node current allocation process. This method reformulates current allocation from a numerical solution problem into a closed-loop voltage-error regulation process. While maintaining stable convergence, it reduces the maximum average iteration order from approximately 105 to within 102. Consequently, the model achieves a real-time ratio of 6.21% under a 5 ms time step with 15 nodes, while maintaining a real-time ratio of 47.2% even under a 1 ms time step with 20 nodes. These results indicate that the model satisfies the real-time execution criterion under the tested millisecond-level time steps and node configurations. Hardware-in-the-loop tests further show that the model can maintain stable real-time operation during dynamic electrical interaction and output continuous dynamic responses of multi-physics state variables. To ensure fidelity, Sobol global sensitivity analysis is employed to reduce the number of uncertain parameters from 15 to 8. Data calibration is then conducted under 12 experimental conditions, keeping the cell voltage prediction error within 5%. Finally, the non-uniform distributions of internal electric, fluid, and thermal fields captured by the model provide a reference for understanding the coupled multi-physics evolution inside the cell. The proposed framework balances physical explainability, computational efficiency, and predictive accuracy, thereby offering a feasible solution for digital twin applications and real-time control strategy optimization of solid oxide cells. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Abstract: This study proposes a reinforcement learning-based dynamic evacuation guidance system for fire emergencies in multi-story buildings. The proposed framework integrates a cellular automata-based fire simulation with an agent-based evacuation simulation to model the coupled dynamics of fire spread and occupant movement. The fire simulation represents the spatiotemporal propagation of flames and smoke, including inter-floor spread through vertical shafts and the stack effect. The evacuation simulation models occupant behavior by incorporating walking speed reductions caused by smoke and crowd density, as well as probabilistic route choice using a mixed logit model to capture heterogeneous decision-making. Within this environment, a reinforcement learning agent dynamically controls directional restrictions at corridor junctions and exits. The agent observes crowd flow, crowd density, fire hazard scores, and exit information, and learns an evacuation guidance policy that minimizes both evacuation time and fatalities through interaction with the simulation environment. To ensure the relevance of the learned policy under realistic deployment conditions, the agent is additionally trained under a sensor uncertainty wrapper that models hazard-sensor noise, CCTV pedestrian detection misses, and measurement latency. Experiments were conducted on a three-story model under 26 fire scenarios with varying ignition locations, with all reinforcement learning agents evaluated under the full sensor uncertainty environment and compared against two deterministic baselines—a rule-based dynamic guidance and a strengthened shortest-path-based baseline that incorporates global path information. The proposed uncertainty-aware policy achieves average reductions of approximately 32% in total evacuation time and 58% in fatalities compared with the rule-based dynamic guidance, and approximately 20% and 42% in the same metrics compared with the strengthened shortest-path-based baseline, with statistical significance confirmed by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction (Holm-adjusted p<0.001). The results demonstrate that reinforcement learning can effectively learn adaptive evacuation guidance policies that consider both fire dynamics and crowd behavior under realistic sensor conditions. These findings support the use of simulation-driven AI decision support as one component of Safety Digital Twin-based safety management for complex buildings. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Uncertainty-aware deep reinforcement learning optimised construction fleet management: A digital twin approach
Affiliations: School of Mechanical Engineering and Mechanics, Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo, China; Faculty of Engineering and Applied Sciences, Cranfield University, Cranfield, United Kingdom; Department of Engineering, Durham University, DH1 3LE, United Kingdom; Faculty of engineering and physical sciences, University of Southampton, Southampton, SO17 1BJ, United Kingdom; School of Aerospace Engineering, Xiamen University, Xiamen, China

Abstract: The construction industry faces great challenges in optimising fleet management under dynamic and uncertain operational conditions. Existing methods either rely on static schedules or heuristic rules, which lack adaptability to uncertain operational conditions and fail to capture the complexity of real-world construction site dynamics, leading to imbalanced resource allocation, disruptions in construction progress, and further deteriorating operational cost uncertainty. This study develops a novel digital twin framework that integrates modelling, simulation, and deep reinforcement learning, specifically the Deep Q-Network (DQN), for optimising fleet management under highly dynamical and uncertain conditions. A simulator of the earthmoving process is developed in the digital world, by modelling the cooperation between excavators and dumpers. By following the physical–virtual–physical workflow of digital twins, real-world data is used to quantify operational parameters and their associated uncertainties. The uncertainties are then integrated into DQN training to generate optimal real-time scheduling strategies, enabled by a new reward design that balances multiple objectives. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed solution offers significant cost savings ranging from 1.41% to 9.71% while ensuring consistent decision-making, even under high uncertainty. This study also discusses how different levels of uncertainty impact operational productivity and costs. This work highlights the potential of the integration of deep reinforcement learning and digital twin approach, emphasising the necessity and impact of incorporating uncertainty in modelling and training to enhance predictive accuracy and decision-making. The proposed framework aims to advance sustainable and intelligent construction practices. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: Advanced Computational Methods for Renewable Energy Forecasting and Electric Vehicle Scheduling: A Literature Review

Abstract: The integration of renewable energy (RE) and electric vehicles (EVs) in power distribution systems creates significant challenges in forecasting accuracy and charging-discharging scheduling under uncertainty. This paper reviews state-of-the-art approaches for renewable energy forecasting and EV scheduling, including machine learning, optimization, uncertainty-aware, and hybrid methods. The review highlights how forecast uncertainty propagates into scheduling decisions and why classical deterministic optimization becomes inadequate at scale. Recent metaheuristic and learning-based strategies that enhance robustness and scalability are analyzed. Key research gaps and future directions are identified, emphasizing explainable AI, digital twins, quantum computing, and blockchain-enabled coordination for practical RE-EV system integration. © 2026 IEEE.
